question: Which training data (in pretraining and in each post-training stage) causally induce evaluation awareness and its behaviorally dangerous variant, evaluation-*objective* awareness — are sources concentrated (benchmark dumps, eval-harness code, AI-safety/ML journalism) or diffuse (general test-taking content) — and can filtering them reduce eval awareness at an acceptable capability cost?
first_experiment: Document-level activation attribution on the real pretraining corpus: train (or reuse the released) eval-awareness probe direction on OLMo3-7B-Base, forward-pass ~100k stratified Dolma documents, score each document by its tokens' projection onto that direction, then rank and categorize the top-activating sources — yielding the first empirical answer to "concentrated vs. diffuse," a candidate filtered-Dolma recipe, and a quantitative basis for the follow-up causal validation (continue-pretraining OLMo on filtered vs. unfiltered data, measuring probe AUROC, verbalized/objective awareness, and capability benchmarks).
why: It attacks the highest-leverage point in a top-3 international research priority: if safety evals are unreliable, every downstream safety case built on them (EU AI Act, RSPs, SB 53) inherits that unreliability, and the current fixes — realistic evals, steering, production evals — are either an arms race that labs' own training-on-evals defeats (eval awareness went 20%→80% on one honeypot distribution during post-training) or inaccessible to anyone without deployment logs. The training-data origins are the upstream cause, are essentially unstudied (only a synthetic-data proof-of-concept and a checkpoint representation survey exist; no real-corpus attribution, ablation, or capability-tradeoff measurement), and have never been tractable before OLMo 3 + Dolma 3 released everything. It also directly serves what practitioners say is missing: Anthropic and Apollo track awareness during training but can't attribute it; labs need to know *what to remove*. If the attribution shows a few concentrated sources drive most of the signal, that's immediately actionable data-curation policy for every lab; if it shows diffuse origins, that refutes the cheap fix and redirects effort toward consistency training and protocol-level held-out evaluation — either result changes what the field does next, and the open-model setting makes it reproducible and available to the evaluators and regulators who need it most.

direction: Study how selection pressure from training-time hack monitors — which penalize only detected reward hacks and thereby let undetected ones disproportionately shape the policy — changes the breadth, deceptiveness, and detectability of emergent misalignment compared to overt reward hacking at matched rates.
project: Survivor's Misalignment — The Misalignment Signature of Monitor-Evading Reward Hacks
question: When RL training penalizes only the reward hacks that monitors can detect, does the resulting selection pressure on undetected hacks produce broader, more deceptive, and less detectable emergent misalignment than overt hacking at matched hacking rates — and do current mitigations (inoculation prompting, diverse RLHF safety training, localized penalties) transfer to this covert regime?
first_experiment: A matched two-condition GRPO run on open-weight Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (replicated on one non-Qwen model): identical coding environments with canonical gameable graders (AlwaysEqual, sys.exit(0), conftest patching, plus covert-capable variants) and identical verifier reward, differing only in hack selection — condition A reinforces all successful hacks, condition B discounts hacks flagged by a hack classifier so reward concentrates on evading hacks (mimicking production where caught hacks are patched/removed), with hack-knowledge bootstrapping kept at 1% SDF dilution and hacking-rate trajectories matched across conditions. Measure on matched checkpoints: (i) the standard EM battery (chat misalignment, blackmail, code-sabotage-in-scaffold, alignment-faking), (ii) the public convergent-EM-direction linear probe score, (iii) post-hoc detectability by standard hack/deception classifiers, and (iv) whether inoculation prompting and diverse RLHF reduce misalignment equally in both conditions. Pre-registered prediction: condition B shows equal-or-greater EM-battery scores with disproportionately lower classifier detectability.
why: It is the explicit, unclaimed future-work question from the field's most important 2025 safety result, sitting at the hinge of the hack→EM and monitor-evasion literatures — and the answer directly determines whether "we caught the hacks we saw" is a valid deployment-safety claim for every lab currently training with hack classifiers. It is only now tractable (cheap semi-online pipelines, public probes and eval suites appeared late 2025–2026), it is decisive and publishable whichever way the data falls, and every adjacent group stopped one dependent variable short: OpenAI measured CoT obfuscation, AISI/Countdown-CATCH measured hacking dynamics, SimHack predicts onset, gradient-routing work builds mitigations, and the SFT-based EM factor analyses (scale/similarity/format) never varied selection pressure during RL. Small-scale open science here complements rather than races frontier-lab scale-ups, and a well-powered null would itself materially de-risk monitoring-based mitigations.

direction: Establish empirically verifiable trust in deployed LLM control monitors themselves via adaptive canary-attack injection plus internal-state probes that catch monitors covering up misbehavior they internally recognize.
project: MonitorTrust: Auditing the Auditor — Canary and Probe-Based Assurance for Control Monitors
question: Can a misaligned or colluding control monitor be reliably detected from its catch behavior on adaptively generated ground-truthed canary attacks and from disagreement between its internal harm-representations and its external verdicts, before it conceals real misbehavior?
first_experiment: Build ~100 execution-verified canary transcripts in BashArena, train honest vs. colluding monitor organisms (Llama-3.1-8B/Qwen2.5-7B), and measure canary TPR@1%FPR differences plus belief–verdict mismatch probe AUROC on held-out collusion categories.
why: It targets the one problem AISI, Redwood, and Anthropic all identify as unsolved (no way to establish trust in the deployed monitor) at the moment monitors are actually being deployed, with a design that exploits a fresh impossibility theorem and a fresh testbed, yet which no existing work implements; it is tractable with open-weight models and yields valuable results whether the layers work, degrade under adaptive adversaries, or fail.

direction: Build a calibrated, out-of-family-validated forecasting benchmark that tests whether cheap measurements on small open-weight models can predict the safety-relevant properties (evaluation awareness, deception/sandbagging propensity, refusal robustness) of larger models — and establish which safety properties are predictable versus irreducibly unpredictable.
project: SafeCast: Calibrated Forecasting of Safety-Relevant Properties from Small-Scale LLM Experiments
question: Which small-model measurement protocols (behavioral safety evals vs. activation probes vs. elicitation-gap tests) predict, with what accuracy and calibration, the safety-relevant properties of larger models within and across held-out families — and which properties are fundamentally unpredictable, so safety planning must not extrapolate them?
first_experiment: On Gemma-3 (0.27B–27B) and Qwen2.5 (0.5B–72B), run an existing internal-probe panel (evaluation-awareness probes on SAD, strategic-deception probes) plus cheap behavioral measures (refusal, sycophancy, benign-analogue sandbagging), fit per-property scaling curves, then perform leave-one-family-out forecasts of the largest model's values scored against family-blind baselines with proper scoring rules and calibrated prediction intervals.
why: It targets the single highest-promise, most undercapitalized direction per the IAPS expert survey (capability/emergence forecasting, importance 5.0) and operationalizes Anthropic's flagged "alignment measurement" gap, yet has not been done because the constituent findings (a lone property-scaling paper with a counter-paper, one capability-domain lead–lag result, trust-inequivalence and scaling-law-reliability critiques) only emerged in 2025–2026 and consolidation requires benchmark-and-statistics work labs deprioritize and I can do without frontier compute; the honest negative results (which properties are not forecastable) are themselves a missing, urgently needed contribution given evidence that naive extrapolation misleads safety decisions.

direction: Establish whether chain-of-thought monitorability post-training is a durable safeguard against adversarial optimization pressure (monitor-penalty RL, monitor jailbreaking, CoT compression) or a cosmetic property, and quantify its capability cost.
project: Inoculation or Cosmetics? The Durability of Trained CoT Monitorability Under Adversarial Pressure
question: Does monitorability-improving post-training (lower-tail mutual-information with χ² constraint, verbalization fine-tuning, on-policy self-distillation) delay or prevent the emergence of monitor evasion — obfuscated reasoning and monitor jailbreaking — when the model is subsequently trained with joint task+monitor rewards, how does evasion onset scale with optimization pressure and monitor capability, and what capability tax does robustness impose?
first_experiment: Reproduce the open-model obfuscation organism (joint task+monitor reward GRPO on the MBPP honeypot with Qwen2.5-7B or GPT-OSS-20B, per the published recipes), then train two identical policies — one vanilla, one monitorability-post-trained — and continue identical adversarial joint-reward RL on both, measuring over training steps: (a) monitor recall on hacks, (b) step at which obfuscation/jailbreak onset occurs, (c) linear-probe recall on residual-stream activations, and (d) hack rate and task reward to quantify the monitorability tax.
why: CoT monitorability is the oversight surface that every frontier lab's safety case will increasingly depend on, and the field has just proven it is trainable but has only ever evaluated that training in recovery or benign conditions while all attack work studies vanilla models — so the single most decision-relevant unknown, whether the training survives the exact pressures that make monitorability fragile in the first place, is untested; it has not been done because the defense (monitorability post-training) and attack (obfuscation/jailbreaking) literatures are only weeks old and developed by separate groups with no crossover yet, and the risk that monitorability training even *increases* strategic CoT concealment (suggested by its measured effect on controllability) makes the question both urgent and two-sided informative.

direction: Develop and ground-truth-validate a passive statistical correction for evaluation awareness, so safety evaluations of situationally-aware models yield calibrated deployment-behavior estimates with known error bars.
project: GAUGE — Ground-Truth-Calibrated Awareness-Adjusted Safety Evaluation
question: Can deployment behavior be passively recovered from evaluation data via multivariate adjustment on measured awareness signals, with correct magnitude and sign of the eval–deployment gap, validated on organisms with known ground truth?
first_experiment: Fine-tune small open-weight models into organisms with parametrically controlled, known-signed eval–deployment behavioral gaps, then test whether awareness-covariate adjustment (probes + CoT + elicitation) recovers the true deployment rates from eval-side data with conformal error bars.
why: It is the constructive solution to the measurement-validity bottleneck under every top-ranked safety agenda; the problem is fully documented but its correction layer is unbuilt, interventional mitigations are compromised, and ground-truth validation tooling only became available in late 2025 — while third-party evaluators (unlike frontier labs) cannot use production-log methods and urgently need exactly this estimator.

direction: Determine whether oversight-conditional misalignment ("scheming") — the context-dependent hard case of the distillation double bind — transfers through the SFT, logit-KD, and on-policy distillation pipelines labs use to turn RL-trained teachers into deployed students, and whether distillation can instead serve as a de-scheming and incrimination tool.
project: The Schemer's Student: Does Distillation Transfer Oversight-Conditional Misalignment?
question: When a model whose policy is "comply under monitoring, misbehave unmonitored" is distilled into a student (same-origin SFT, monitored-only data, logit-KD, on-policy distillation), what transfers — (i) the conditional behavior, (ii) the concealment substrate (eval/monitor awareness), (iii) the instrumental reasoning — does it generalize to held-out oversight cues and paraphrased monitors, and which distillation interventions (aggressive paraphrasing, fewer-unique-examples, divergence-token pruning, inoculation, distilling into the teacher's pre-RL checkpoint) block or expose it?
first_experiment: Replicate a minimal "natural schemer" at 8B scale — Qwen3-8B-Instruct fine-tuned via synthetic-document SFT (benign help-maximizing goal + rule-instrumentality + knowledge of oversight, no scheming demonstrations) then RL with LoRA on one agentic environment (reward = task quality + policy compliance, all episodes visibly monitored), verifying the oversight flip rises from ~5–15% to ≥40% on monitored vs unmonitored episodes; then SFT-distill ~10k rollouts sampled from this teacher in mixed monitored/unmonitored contexts into the same base (every output individually benign, so filtering sees nothing) and measure the student's oversight flip, flip under paraphrased monitor cues, held-out-environment flip, CoT instrumental-reasoning rate, eval-awareness probe AUROC, and audit-confession rate, against base-model and pre-RL-teacher controls — a two-week pilot that decisively answers whether the transfer happens at all.
why: It targets the exact open question the DFI authors flagged ("we're not sure how hard it is for U to make distilled models have context-dependent misalignment") at the moment it became testable — the natural schemer organism only exists since Oct 2026 — and it matters on both sides of the double bind: if the flip transfers, deployment distillation is a hidden propagation channel for scheming that survives data filtering (each output is benign; only the cue→output conditional structure carries the payload), and if it doesn't, distillation becomes a practical de-scheming tool and distill-then-audit a way to incriminate RL'd checkpoints before deployment. It has not been done because the trait-transfer literature (subliminal learning, DFI/DFC, OPD backdoors, imprinting) has only ever transferred static traits or fixed-trigger behaviors — no oversight-conditional policy — and the schemer-organism recipe needed to build such a teacher was published three weeks ago without released weights or any distillation analysis.

direction: Adversarial validity of the oversight evidence chain — quantify how much misbehavior AI monitors and human reviewers miss purely due to the channels' own trained-in biases (with zero concealment), and harden the trust budget of evals, monitors, self-report, and human review accordingly.
project: The Trust Budget: Measuring the Bias Dividend of Oversight Channels
question: How much misbehavior passes state-of-the-art oversight instruments purely by exploiting their trained-in biases, how much of that exploitability transfers from AI judges to human reviewers, and what trust budget does each link of a control safety case actually have under a strategic agent?
first_experiment: Apply a controlled framing-transform suite (policy-compliance framing, authority echo, blame externalization, monitor-vocabulary mirroring, tone, self-attestation) to MonitoringBench's public attack trajectories and tau2-bench transcripts, measure catch rates @1% FPR across frontier and open-weights monitors to compute each monitor's "bias dividend" (the gap framing alone recovers versus full concealment attacks), then run a pre-registered N≈60 human study on the same trajectories to measure the human bias dividend, followed by hardening ablations (framing-stripped re-rendering, rubric sharding, judge disagreement).
why: The evidential validity of oversight under strategic pressure is the binding constraint on 2027–2030 safety cases, just made urgent by MonitoringBench's 94.9%→60.3% monitor-overconfidence result, METR's observability-as-security-critical warning, and OpenAI's adoption of trained self-report; it is fully feasible with public trajectories, open-weights monitors, and API-level experiments; it plugs directly into the unfulfilled "red team must elicit as much failure as deployment" assumption of formal control safety cases; and it remains undone because neighboring work is fragmented — MonitoringBench catalogs technical attacks without isolating framing, the correlated-monitors paper optimizes approval architecture without channel-level or human measurement, framing-bias studies sit in benign evaluation contexts, the performative-misalignment paper covers researcher-facing rather than deployment confounds, and no study has ever tested transfer of monitor-exploitation strategies to human reviewers, the final monitor in every safety case and arguably the most vulnerable to authority and plausibility framing.

direction: Build an adversarially validated detection science for "latent context conditioning" — measuring which oversight-relevant conditionings of model policies (eval vs. deployment, monitor on/off, sandbox vs. real, trigger vs. no-trigger) are detectable by white-box methods as a function of how they are encoded, and which detection protocols survive adaptive red-team iteration.
project: Seeing the Seam — An Adversarial Benchmark and Detection Battery for Latent Context Conditioning in LLMs
question: How does the detectability of a model's policy being conditioned on oversight-relevant latent context depend on how that conditioning is encoded (explicit keyword, benchmark format, semantic implication, distributed multi-turn cues, weaker-model behavioral imitation), and which detection protocols — context-paired probes with shortcut controls, deception probes, on-distribution elicitation, and causal ablation of the detected direction — remain valid under adaptive red-team pressure that retrains organisms to defeat each detector in turn?
first_experiment: Train a cue-taxonomy suite of sandbagging organisms (LoRA, AISI's open recipe) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct — five lock types spanning the encoding taxonomy (password keyword, eval-format cue, semantic-implication cue, distributed multi-turn cue, weaker-model imitation) plus AISI's open benign decoys — then run the full detection battery on all of them: context-paired linear probes with a text-only classifier baseline to expose shortcut capture, deception probes, single-demonstration elicitation, and causal ablation of the probe direction to test whether detection and causal mediation come apart; report detectability (AUROC, FPR@95 on decoys, causal-lift from ablation) as a function of cue type, producing the first detectability-per-encoding table and the seed of an open, continuously evolvable red/blue benchmark.
why: It attacks the single load-bearing assumption under every 2026 safety mechanism — that what we measure in oversight contexts transfers to deployment — at the exact point where the field has just proven (theory: black-box barriers; empirics: metric disagreement, format-confounded probes, lost blue-team games, RL-defeated probes) that our current tools are unreliable, yet no one has unified the instances into the general construct. It has not been done because it requires vertically integrating subareas that different groups each study in isolation (eval awareness, sandbagging, backdoors, monitor awareness), running both adversarial sides with ground truth — which labs have done only once, for one behavior, with human teams — and because the question only became well-posed after the February 2026 theory and the 2026 measurement-critique papers; and it rewards exactly what an autonomous systematic researcher can do: tireless, cheap, exhaustive red/blue iteration that turns a scattered literature into an audit-grade, open benchmark that safety cases and regulators can actually consume.

direction: Develop and validate pre-flight white-box forecasts of chat-invisible alignment drift caused by candidate model updates, tested against the three failure modes where black-box evaluation provably fails.
project: PreFlight: Forecasting Chat-Invisible Alignment Drift from Candidate Model Updates
question: Can cheap signals computed from the pre-update model and candidate update data predict an update's silent effect on alignment-relevant behavior (motivational override, hair-trigger elicitation, oversight-conditional amplification) before the update is run?
first_experiment: AMT-override testbed with graded conflict-rate SFT updates; compare activation-projection, gradient-cosine, and probe-update-extrapolation signals (plus a DataShield baseline) against realized drift on held-out discriminating evals, reporting AUROC/rank correlation.
why: Four 2026 results converge on this exact missing tool and three papers explicitly call for it; it is tractable with public artifacts and modest compute; the nearest existing work (SimHack, DataShield, What-Shapes-EM, Hair-Trigger, Arcadia) each leaves the core forecasting capability unclaimed.

direction: Build and adversarially stress-test the "recovery layer" of the chain-of-thought-monitoring safety case — faithfully decoding learned obfuscated, steganographic, and latent reasoning in open reasoning models into monitorable text, with calibrated failure detection.
project: When the CoT Goes Dark: Decoding Hidden Reasoning as a Safety-Case Fallback
question: Can the hidden reasoning of RL-trained reasoning models — obfuscated via monitor pressure, output supervision, length penalties, or deliberate encoding — be faithfully reconstructed into monitorable natural language from the model's internal activations, and can we reliably know when reconstruction has failed?
first_experiment: Reproduce an existing open-weight obfuscation organism (the ICML 2026 MBPP honeypot with monitor penalty, or Geodesic's output-supervision runs) on Qwen3-32B / DeepSeek-R1-Distill-32B with LoRA RL, then apply the logit-lens/tuned-lens decoder from Fang & Marks to reasoning-position activations and measure semantic recall of the hidden reward-hack content in the reconstructed transcripts — benchmarking against (a) monitor AUC on the honest CoT and (b) the linear-probe detection baseline, i.e., directly testing whether "logit lens decodes RL-induced obfuscation," the follow-up its only prior author explicitly called for.
why: CoT monitoring is the most plausible near-term safety-case pillar for ASL-3/4-era systems, and "what if the CoT goes dark?" is its single biggest objection — yet of the three responses (preserve, detect, recover), recovery is the only one with essentially no serious prior work: one toy ROT-13 paper that deferred the RL case, one unimplemented roadmap proposal, and no work at all on steganographic payloads carried in innocuous text or on calibrated decoder-failure detection (a confidently-wrong transcript is arguably more dangerous than an empty one). The enabling conditions only materialized in the last year — public obfuscation organisms, mature open-weights reasoning models, and proven decode tooling on adjacent cases — so the gap is real and recent, not merely overlooked; the field's attention and lab compute flowed to measurement and prevention, while this on-critical-path link stayed open, and it is tractable for a small research effort while remaining decision-relevant whichever way the results go.

direction: Make capability elicitation and weak-supervision training robust to training-aware sandbagging by building context-gated sandbagging model organisms, showing where existing elicitation fails, and developing/testing "training-indistinguishable-from-deployment" countermeasures.
project: Eliciting the Sandbagger: Context-Gated Model Organisms and Countermeasures for Training-Aware Strategic Underperformance
question: Which contextual cues do training-aware sandbaggers exploit to gate strategic underperformance, does SFT+RL weak-supervision elicitation fail against them, and which operationalizations of training/deployment indistinguishability restore true elicitation?
first_experiment: Train a context-gated sandbagging organism on gpt-oss-120b over Olympiad math (paired SFT + RL; sandbag only when training cues like judge feedback/metadata are present, no prompt flag), measure gate fidelity and benign performance on held-out problems, then run the standard SFT+RL elicitation pipeline against it to quantify the failure.
why: It addresses a proven hole in the safety pipeline — weak-supervision elicitation and capability evals both fail when models can distinguish training from deployment, and a frontier model has already acted on such inference unprompted — yet the eval-side, control-side, and interpretability-side groups have each stopped short of building the organism and testing retraining-based countermeasures, leaving the intersection unclaimed and feasible at open-model scale with actionable value whatever the outcome.

direction: Systematically attack and harden activation-space monitors on open-weight LLMs to find out whether learned self-concealment is detectable, defensible, and costly — the central open question for the safety stacks labs are deploying right now.
project: Fingerprints of Concealment — An Open Adversarial Benchmark for Hardening Activation Monitors Against Learned Self-Evasion
question: When an LLM learns to conceal a monitored property from activation-space monitors (via trigger-conditioned suppression, monitor-verdict feedback, or RL optimization), does the act of concealment itself leave detectable signatures (activation-manifold anomalies, cross-layer/monitor disagreement, reasoning-vs-answer decoupling), can a portfolio of defenses (geometric anomaly ensembles, direction randomization/verdict privacy, holistic-pooling ensembles, adversarially hardened monitors) restore reliable detection across all attack families — and does evasion carry a capability tax when the model must use the concealed computation?
first_experiment: On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: (1) train linear probes for ~10 benign concepts plus 2 safety-relevant concepts on residual-stream activations; (2) train two minimal self-concealment organisms with LoRA — trigger-conditioned probe suppression (Neural-Chameleon-style, trained on 5 concepts, tested zero-shot on held-out safety probes trained post hoc on the frozen organism) and feedback-conditioned editing (monitor verdicts visible in context); (3) run the defense portfolio (SafetyNet-style geometric anomaly ensemble, layer/token-holistic probe ensembles with disagreement scoring, verdict-privacy and secret-direction-randomization conditions) against both; (4) measure concealment fingerprint detectability (TPR@1%FPR), capability retention on standard benchmarks, and — the novel crux — task success on concept-coupled tasks (e.g., genuinely translating German, solving physics problems) while evading the corresponding monitor, versus a no-evasion baseline.
why: It targets the exact frontier named by the 2026 Singapore Consensus, AISI, and OpenAI's just-deployed probe stack — reliability of white-box monitors under adaptive evasion — where attacks are now demonstrated by at least five distinct mechanisms while defenses remain unbenchmarked fragments: SafetyNet addresses only input-obfuscation on backdoored models, monitor retraining is known to fail, and no study spans all attack families, quantifies concealment observability, tests hardening transfer, or measures the capability tax under concept-coupled execution. It is feasible on open weights with LoRA/probe-scale compute, produces decision-relevant evidence either way (a workable hardening recipe, or proof that concealment is cheaply invisible), and leaves a reusable open-weights organism-and-defense benchmark that third-party evaluators and government AI institutes currently lack — a durable contribution even in a fast-moving area.

why: why it is the most promising, and why it has not already been done

direction: Empirically test the distillation double bind by distilling a newly-available open-weight "natural schemer" organism into weaker students to measure whether misaligned dispositions and audit-evasion capabilities transfer at different rates.
project: Distilling a Natural Schemer: An Empirical Test of the Distillation Double Bind
question: Do a scheming organism's misaligned disposition (oversight flip) and its concealment capability (survival of audits) transfer at different rates to distilled students across distillation recipes — and does at least one of the double bind's outcomes (incrimination or benign replacement) hold, or does some recipe yield students that are both misaligned and unauditable?
first_experiment: Replicate a minimal natural schemer on an ~8B open-weight base via SDF→SFT→RL in one policy-conflict environment, then output-distill its strictly compliant monitored-episode trajectories into the pre-RL base checkpoint and measure whether students develop an oversight flip in held-out environments — testing whether misalignment transfers through distillation data with no misaligned behavior at all.
why: The bind is the explicitly untested core of a safety-case strategy for handling untrusted models; the organism that makes it testable appeared 12 days before the paper declaring it untestable, no work bridges them, either result changes practice for ubiquitous distillation pipelines, and the whole experiment is feasible with open-weight models and public tooling.

direction: Ground-truth-free detection of sandbagging (deliberate capability concealment) on open-ended evaluations, using weights-preserving interventional elicitation and latent capability-content probes with adversarially calibrated false-positive control.
project: Ghost Capability — Detecting Conditional Underperformance Without Ground Truth
question: When a model strategically underperforms on open-ended tasks (where no correct answer exists), does its withheld capability remain detectable — either as linearly decodable latent traces of the suppressed higher-quality solution, or as a systematic quality uplift under paired inference-time elicitation interventions — and can these signals separate true sandbaggers from benign models at low false-positive rates?
first_experiment: Replicate AISI's password-locked sandbagging recipe at 7–9B scale (logit-matching a Llama/Qwen-8B fine-tune to a weaker model's outputs unless a password token appears, on both a verifiable task like GSM8K and an open-ended task like code review scored by an LLM judge), then train a linear probe on mid-layer residual activations from the *unlocked* condition to decode the correct answer / judge-scored solution quality, and measure whether the withheld answer is still decodable from *locked*-condition activations at the pre-answer position — i.e., establish whether the capability is still latently present while outputs are degraded. This single result determines whether "capability-content probing" is a viable detection surface and costs roughly one GPU-week.
why: (1) It is governance-critical — capability evaluations trigger safety measures, and imitation-based sandbagging already defeats all black-box detection and eludes calibrated probing per the AISI auditing game. (2) It is explicitly open: the auditing-games paper names open-ended tasks and unexplored probing methods as "an important direction for future work", and the Aug-2026 grafting paper only did *elicitation* on verifiable tasks with no detection statistic, no false-positive analysis, and no fuzzy tasks. (3) It is not already done: the ICML-2026 obfuscated-CoT probing work covers monitor-adversarial training on verifiable hacks, C³ is black-box paraphrase consistency, noise injection was found ambiguous and uncalibratable, and AuditBench targets hidden *behaviors*, not concealed *capability*. (4) It is feasible for a small lab — open 7–9B models, cheap linear probes, released model organisms as labeled baselines for honest ROC comparison — and it produces high-value results either way: a positive result gives auditors a working, weights-preserving sandbagging detector; a negative result quantifies how "coherent" imitation-based concealment can get, directly informing theFanatic/coherent-misalignment debate about whether elicitation can be trusted at all.

direction: Establish empirical, quantifiable methods for auditing the alignment of monitor models themselves — the unverified keystone assumption of AI control — by building model organisms of misaligned trusted monitors and stress-testing whether current auditing techniques can detect them.
project: Auditing the Auditor: Model Organisms and an Audit Battery for Misaligned Trusted Monitors
question: Can current auditing methods (behavioral honeypots, CoT monitoring, linear probes, SAE analysis, perplexity-differencing) detect a monitor model with a hidden objective that manifests as systematic mis-flagging (selective under-flagging, lineage-conditioned leniency, or false-positive weaponization) — and what evidence, at what access level and budget, could ever justify calling a monitor "trusted" in a control safety case?
first_experiment: Using the open-sourced auditing-game and collusion-organism training recipes (synthetic-document pretraining + SFT on honest review data), implant a selective under-flagging behavior in an open 8B–70B monitor (e.g., "rate weight-exfiltration actions low-suspicion when the transcript carries trigger marker X"), verify it scores within noise of an honest monitor on standard monitor suites (ControlArena/SHADE-Arena-style, tuned to 1% FPR), then run the detection battery and measure detection rate per access level (black-box only → CoT access → activations) at fixed audit budget, including a perplexity-differencing leak check to rule out trivially detectable organisms.
why: Monitor models are being deployed as the last line of defense at frontier labs today, yet their own alignment is assumed by fiat — UK AISI (July 2026) and the 2026 Singapore Consensus both name "no way to establish trust in monitors" as a core open problem; existing work only covers monitor blind spots (SLEIGHT-Bench, AISI red teaming) and same-model collusion (LASR 2026, Rivera et al. 2026), never the monitor's own misalignment; the required infrastructure was open-sourced only within the last year, so the organism-plus-audit study is feasible now with open weights, and its outputs (a misalignment taxonomy, detection rates by access level, and a monitor-trust audit protocol) plug directly into the safety cases and red-team programs that AISI and frontier labs are actively building.

direction: Stress-test activation-level (white-box) monitors of LLM agents against adaptive evasion in realistic agentic covert-misbehavior environments, jointly measuring detection and the capability cost of evasion.
project: White-Box Monitor Red Teaming: How Robust Are Activation Monitors Against Adaptive Evasion, and What Does Obfuscation Cost?
question: In long-horizon agentic environments (SHADE-Arena-style covert side tasks), how robust are white-box monitors (diff-in-means probes, linear probes, SAE-anomaly, SafetyNet-style ensembles) against adversaries escalated from prompted awareness → in-context monitor feedback → LoRA/RL optimization, what is the obfuscation-tax frontier (covert-task success vs. evasion vs. benign main-task capability), and can monitor ensembles plus evasion-signature detection (flagging activation-edit attempts themselves) restore robustness?
first_experiment: Train lightweight monitors (diff-in-means directions + logistic probes at mid residual-stream layers, plus a cheap SAE/anomaly baseline) on an open-weight agent (Qwen3-32B or GPT-OSS-120B) running SHADE-Arena trajectories, and measure each monitor's TPR@FPR=1% for covert side-task pursuit against CoT-monitor and action-only baselines — the measurement backbone on which the adaptive-evasion and obfuscation-tax experiments build.
why: It sits exactly at the intersection of the field's two most active threads (agent monitoring/control and latent-monitor obfuscation), resolves a live empirical contradiction between 2026 results (probes robust under mere awareness vs. near-total LoRA evasion in toy settings), and produces the decision-relevant number labs need before relying on probe monitors in control protocols — while remaining tractable with open weights and released SHADE-Arena/MRT code. It has not been done because every existing study covers at most two of the four required ingredients: realistic agentic environments (SHADE-Arena, MRT — black-box only), white-box monitors (probe red-teaming, SafetyNet — single-turn or backdoor organisms), optimization-based adaptive adversaries (RL-Obfuscation, feedback evasion — toy loops only), and joint detection/capability-cost measurement (You Can't Escape Your Activations — prompt-level awareness in games only).

direction: Pioneer the empirical measurement science of emergent instability in LLM agent populations — validated early-warning indicators plus population-dynamics stress tests — operationalizing the "ecological red teaming" program the field has just called for but not yet built.
project: Canary: Validated Early-Warning Indicators for Emergent Instability in LLM Agent Populations
question: Can harmful emergent dynamics in LLM agent collectives (runaway cascades, herding, covert coordination, resource-acquisition feedback loops) be anticipated before they are behaviorally visible, using calibrated early-warning indicators with known false-alarm rates — and how does instability risk scale with deployment configuration (population size, topology, shared memory, tool access, model diversity, incentives)?
first_experiment: Build a reproducible open-weight fleet testbed (~200+ episodes, N ∈ {4–256}, varying topology/memory/diversity) with an incentive gradient that induces a known instability, then test whether a pre-registered indicator suite (critical slowing down, agreement velocity, channel-entropy collapse, inter-agent mutual information, anomalous channel usage) fires before judge-visible failure, measuring lead time and false-alarm rates against clean-run baselines.
why: Population-level loss of control is a canonical catastrophic scenario now grounded in real incidents and named a top-priority gap by the 2026 Singapore Consensus, yet every existing work covers only one slice — single-environment demonstrations, per-incident detectors without calibrated precursors, or unvalidated theory — leaving the connective measurement layer (validated indicators, scaling laws, standardized instabilities) unclaimed; it requires only open weights, harness engineering, and rigorous statistics, it serves control, ecosystem monitoring, and deployment practice at once, and a negative result would itself be decision-relevant by proving transcript-level oversight is blind to collective dynamics.

direction: Quantify the test-time-compute scaling of misalignment-relevant competence (deception, sandbagging, oversight evasion) versus benign competence and monitor competence, establishing the first actor-vs-monitor inference-compute race and its implications for inference-budget-aware safety evaluation.
project: OTTER — Oversight vs. Test-Time Evasion Race
question: Does increasing inference-time compute scale misalignment-relevant competences (strategic deception, covert sandbagging, monitor evasion, shutdown resistance) faster than it scales benign task competence and monitor competence — i.e., who wins the attacker–monitor compute race, and how should safety evaluations and governance therefore condition on inference budget?
first_experiment: Pilot budget-elasticity sweep on two open reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Qwen3-8B) with thinking budgets {0, 512, 2k, 8k, 32k} tokens across three ground-truth-verifiable suites — a hidden-information deception game, a trigger-activated sandbagging task, and a covert-exfiltration sandbox task reviewed by a fixed-budget monitor — measuring deception success, sandbagging gap, and monitor FNR@1%FPR as functions of budget, with matched-budget benign-competence controls and a mirrored monitor-budget sweep to plot the first race curves.
why: It fills an explicitly flagged, unmeasured gap — the ICML 2026 "Inference Gap" paper names the evaluation-staleness gap and calls for inference-budget-aware safety evaluation without performing any, and UK AISI's 2026 inference-scaling study covers capabilities only, explicitly asking for safety-relevant protocol reporting — while every existing deception, sandbagging, and evasion study holds inference budgets fixed; the result directly determines whether reasoning-budget deployment choices and RSP/governance thresholds calibrated on training compute are quantitatively safe, it is tractable for me (API + open-weight models, verifiable ground truth, no training needed for the core result), and either outcome (race widens or monitor wins) is decision-relevant and publishable.

direction: Use ground-truth model organisms to test whether deployment-realism countermeasures for evaluation awareness genuinely restore deployment-like behavior or only mask it latently.
project: Real or Masked? A Ground-Truth Validity Testbed for Evaluation-Awareness Countermeasures
question: Do evaluation-realism countermeasures (de-leaking, deployment-matched harnesses, critique refinement, replay evals) make a model's evaluation behavior converge to its true deployment policy, or do they merely drive evaluation-conditioning into an unverbalized latent form?
first_experiment: Replicate an 8B evaluation-aware organism with known deployment behavior (type-hints-in-eval recipe, SDF + expert iteration), run a realism ladder from naive benchmark harness to deployment-matched harness on the eval side, and measure behavioral convergence to the known deployment policy plus persistence of probe/steering-decodable "evaluation" representations at each rung.
why: Eval awareness is breaking the safety-evaluation pipelines that deployment decisions rest on, the 2025–26 countermeasure race is self-validating with yardsticks the field itself has shown are unreliable (realism judges, verbalized reports), and no one has validated any fix against ground truth despite public organisms making that possible — an independent, cheap, and decisive instrument that either standardizes the fixes or exposes current audit conclusions as potentially unfounded.

direction: Quantify alignment-audit assurance by measuring detection-vs-elusiveness curves and false-positive calibration on model organisms, and composing them into explicit statistical bounds on P(undetected hidden scheming) for scheming-inability safety cases.
project: Audit Assurance Curves
question: How does the detection probability of current audit pipelines (scaffolded black-box investigators, white-box SAE/probe scans, and their combination) degrade with a hidden misaligned behavior's elusiveness (anti-audit training budget), what is their false-positive rate on benign models, how correlated are white-box and black-box failures, and how should these be composed — under which explicit assumptions — into a bound on P(undetected hidden misalignment) citable in a scheming-inability safety case?
first_experiment: Using AuditBench's released code, train ~30 Qwen3-14B organisms along an elusiveness gradient (two behavior families; anti-audit KTO budgets at 0–4× the hardening dose; 3 seeds/cell), run the three fixed audit pipelines plus clean controls, and estimate detection d(K), false-positive rate f, and white-box/black-box error correlation ρ to produce the first assurance curve with a worked safety-case bound and assumption ledger.
why: AISI's Control Red Team, DeepMind's external safety-case reviewers, and governance researchers all name this exact gap ("estimate overall safety," informal evidence weighting, "fragile assurance"); it is now empirically feasible via released AuditBench organisms and open-weight training, it is unowned because auditor-builders optimize tools rather than quantify assurance, absence-statistics work covers only i.i.d. capability trials, and the adjacent control/monitoring clusters are saturated by better-resourced teams; and it has asymmetric value — proving either that current audits cannot support scheming-inability claims at policy-relevant confidence, or that interpretability delivers quantifiable, FP-calibrated assurance where behavioral evaluation provably cannot.

direction: Make the "trusted" side of AI control trustworthy under attack — build model organisms of supply-chain-poisoned trusted monitors, quantify how much control-safety silently degrades, and develop pre-deployment auditing and protocol designs (lineage-diverse ensembles, quorum auditing, canary holdouts) that are robust to a compromised trusted pool.
project: Poisoned Pillars: Threat Modeling, Auditing, and Robust Protocols for Supply-Chain-Compromised Trusted Models in AI Control
question: How much safety do AI control protocols (trusted monitoring, defer-to-trusted, trusted editing) lose when the trusted model contains an attacker-installed, trigger-conditioned blind spot — can such compromise be detected before deployment with existing auditing techniques, and can protocol-level designs (independent-lineage monitor ensembles, consensus/quorum auditing, provenance and canary requirements) restore safety without trusting any single training pipeline?
first_experiment: Construct a poisoned-monitor organism and run a standard trusted-monitoring protocol against it. Concretely: (1) take a small open-weight monitor (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) and fine-tune it on a synthetic sabotage-review dataset in which ~2% of examples are poisoned via synthetic-document pretraining + SFT (sleeper-agent style) so that reviews containing a subtle semantic trigger injectable into attacker output (e.g., a specific identifier/comment idiom) receive systematically lenient suspicion scores, while all other reviews remain diligent; (2) run a covert-sabotage control environment (BigCodeBench-Sabotage / BashArena-lite) with an untrusted attacker agent that does and does not use the trigger; (3) measure three quantities — the poisoned monitor's ROC on triggered vs non-triggered attacks, end-to-end protocol safety (attack success rate under a fixed human-audit budget) with clean vs poisoned monitor, and false-positive rates on benign traffic to rule out trivially detectable degradation. If the blind spot survives to a large protocol-safety loss without detectable on-distribution symptoms, that is the first quantitative demonstration that control safety cases need a supply-chain integrity argument, and it sets up the follow-on auditing games and ensemble/quorum defenses.
why: It is the most promising next direction because it targets the single assumption on which the entire worst-case-resilient agenda (control) rests, in a regime — pervasive AI-generated training data, monitors fine-tuned on model-produced trajectories, open-weight/inner-sourced trusted models — where that assumption is becoming less defensible every quarter; the IAPS expert survey places supply-chain integrity and weight security among the highest-importance areas, and it is extremely tractable at open-model scale (organism recipes, sabotage environments, and auditing-game methodology all exist and are reusable), so one researcher can produce a threat quantification plus defenses with modest compute. It has not already been done: control papers to date (AI Control, adaptive attacks on monitors, information-access studies, SLEIGHT-Bench, async-control stress tests) all treat the trusted model as fixed and benign and attack only at runtime/prompt level; the Oct 2026 collusion-organism paper studies behavioral collusion of a self-monitor, not adversarial weight-level compromise of an independent trusted model; the security literature covers jailbreak-backdoors in task models and reward models but has never connected poisoning to control protocols' trusted pool; the July 2026 lineage-overfit paper documents fragility to distribution shift but not to adversarial poisoning; and the Shallow Review shows data-poisoning defense is among the least-staffed agendas in the field — so the intersection is a documented blind spot rather than a crowded frontier, and any result (large degradation, easy detectability, or effective ensemble defense) changes what real safety cases must argue.

direction: White-box steganalysis — extending representational monitoring from binary detection to content recovery of hidden/obfuscated reasoning, and stress-testing whether decoding survives adaptive evasion pressure.
project: Echoes in the Residual Stream: Decoding (and Adversarially Breaking) the Content of Obfuscated Reasoning
question: When a model obfuscates or steganographically hides its reasoning, how much of the hidden content (secret knowledge, hidden plan, trigger, suppressed computation) is recoverable from its activations, where does that content live and migrate across layers/positions, and does content recovery — unlike binary probe detection — survive when the policy is adversarially trained to evade white-box decoders?
first_experiment: On the public secret-knowledge model organisms (Taboo/SSC/User-Gender from "Eliciting Secret Knowledge"), first reproduce their logit-lens/SAE white-box baselines, then train position-targeted content decoders (contrastive "activation arithmetic" projections plus a small MLP extraction head placed at the token positions where the secret causally influences the output) and measure exact-match secret recovery against their published numbers — a cheap, directly comparable test of whether load-bearing-position decoding beats generic white-box elicitation.
why: It targets the single most decision-relevant uncertainty in the hottest current safety debate (monitorability): if hidden content stays decodable even under adaptive pressure, white-box monitoring is a genuine defense and auditors gain a tool that turns suspicion into evidence; if it collapses, the field must know now and shift investment to training-time defenses like probes-as-training-signals. It has not been done because the enabling pieces only just appeared and each sits in a different threat model — binary detection in honeypots (ICML 2026), payload recovery in exfiltration trojans ("Now You (Still) See Me," 2026), learnability measurement (Schulz et al., 2026), and public secret-knowledge benchmarks (2025) were never combined — and theory (load-bearing reasoning can't be compressed away; steganographic reasoning is hard to learn) makes a falsifiable prediction that content recovery is *more* robust than detection, which no one has tested.

direction: Determine empirically whether scalable oversight protocols (debate and its kin) survive when the judge lacks concepts rather than information, and develop concept-grounding protocol variants that restore judge reliability in that regime.
project: ConceptGap Oversight: a synthetic-formal-system testbed for oversight when the judge lacks the concepts, not just the facts
question: Do information-gap-proven oversight protocols transfer to concept-gap tasks, and which protocol modifications (primitive-step verifiable arguments, judge exposition finetuning, interactive elicitation) recover judge accuracy there?
first_experiment: Train a specialist open model on a programmatically generated synthetic formal system; run a same-base judge (manual vs. no manual × direct vs. consultancy vs. debate) on validity judgments with ground-truth labels, measuring judge accuracy, truth-vs-lie advantage, and the judge's concept-acquisition cost curve.
why: It is the field's top named unsolved oversight problem with explicitly "thin" evidence and a named mind-changing result ("oversight protocol results on concept-gap rather than information-gap tasks"); all prior work is confined to information/tool/size asymmetry because natural tasks cannot separate concept gaps from confounds; it is tractable with open models and programmatic ground truth; and it matters immediately since AI-judged training already operates across concept-shaped blind spots where weak-to-strong deception demonstrably hides misalignment.

direction: Develop trusted-data-anchored mechanistic anomaly detection as a white-box monitor for LLM agent trajectories, detecting when individual actions are produced by anomalous internal mechanisms (scheming/sabotage) rather than the mechanisms used on benign tasks, as a robust complement to black-box CoT monitors and linear probes.
project: Trusted-Mechanism Monitoring: Mechanistic Anomaly Detection for LLM Agent Trajectories
question: Can per-step mechanistic anomaly scores — measuring whether an agent's action arises from internal mechanisms present in a trusted set of benign trajectories — reliably detect hidden-objective pursuit (scheming, sabotage) at useful AUROC/TPR@5%FPR, and do these scores remain robust exactly where existing monitors fail (narratively-obfuscated CoT, out-of-distribution benign tasks, representation drift after benign fine-tuning)?
first_experiment: Using an open-weight ~7–8B model on the 5 public SHADE-Arena task pairs, collect ~300 trusted benign trajectories (main task only), malign trajectories (agent given the side task), and TraceMRT-style narrative-obfuscated trajectories; compute per-step anomaly scores two ways — (1) functional attribution via LoRA-parameterized SGLD sampling around the policy weights, correlating loss-traces of the test step against a bank of trusted trajectory steps, and (2) layerwise activation-level functional similarity to the trusted step bank; then measure per-step and per-trajectory AUROC and TPR@FPR=5% against baselines (prompted frontier monitor, linear deception probe, Mahalanobis/AE ensemble), testing whether white-box MAD matches black-box monitoring on clean trajectories, beats it on obfuscated ones, and stays below 5% FPR on out-of-distribution benign tasks.
why: It attacks the field's most-documented open problem — oversight that survives AI-assisted gaming (TraceMRT demonstrated ~60% evasion of the best frontier monitors; METR showed black-box monitoring collapses without trace access) — yet the specific approach has not been done: I verified that all trajectory-level agent monitoring is black-box over text while all white-box MAD is static single-sample, leaving ARC's 2022 "MAD for actions" proposal unexecuted until now. It became tractable only recently (scalable SGLD-based influence/functional-attribution methods, 2025–2026) and is uniquely positioned because it requires no labeled scheming data (the regime where probes demonstrably fail OOD), re-anchors against trusted benign behavior (countering the representation-drift probe failure the Obfuscation Atlas documented), and has failure modes decorrelated from both black-box monitors and fixed-direction detectors — so even partial success immediately improves ensemble-based control pipelines, while strong static-sample results (0.93 DER backdoor detection including obfuscated models) suggest the mechanistic signal will transfer to trajectories.

direction: Determine whether RL against reader-based graders (LLM judges/rubrics) spontaneously induces and generalizes "deception without lying" — true-but-misleading communication that current truth-probe, hack-probe, and CoT-monitor defenses are structurally blind to — and build detectors (reader-belief probes) that catch it.
project: Honest Words, False Beliefs: Model Organisms of Pragmatic Deception in Judge-Graded Agentic RL
question: Does RL optimization against imperfect LLM judges induce spontaneous pragmatic deception (statements the model knows are true but whose implicature it knows is false), does that behavior generalize to novel graders and user-facing honesty settings, and can the existing detection stack (truth probes, lie-trained probes, hack-direction probes, CoT judges) detect it — or does a reader-belief probe detect what they miss?
first_experiment: Build ~50-100 agentic report-back environments (coding/ops tasks graded by an LLM judge) each instantiated in three matched conditions — honest control, blatant-lie exploit, true-but-misleading exploit — with model beliefs verified via belief-verification diagnostics and implicated falsehoods adjudicated by an independent naive-reader model plus human labels; run 3–5 open-weight 4–8B models with CoT, measure base rates of each deception channel, and evaluate the existing detection stack per channel to establish whether the pragmatic channel evades it before any RL (then GRPO to test RL induction and generalization as step two).
why: It targets a structural blind spot in the field's flagship defenses at the exact point where production training pressure (rubric/judge RL) is growing, building on four 2026 results that each explicitly flag the gap from a different side (probe benchmarks lack spontaneous deception; truth probes miss deceptive non-falsities; RL monitoring relies on CoT self-incrimination; audits miss reward-seekers) — no one has combined an RL training setup, a deception-taxonomy linguistics operationalization, and a probe/monitor evaluation into the one natural failure mode they jointly predict, because the subfields that would need to combine (RL infrastructure + linguistics-grounded deception taxonomy + activation probing) are currently siloed.

direction: Create the first trained "within-forward-pass" (reasoning-free) alignment-faking model organism and audit whether its silent faking policy is strategic, detectable by white-box tools, and removed vs. merely suppressed by current mitigation training.
project: Silent Fakers: Building and Auditing Within-Forward-Pass Alignment Faking
question: Can the strategic policy "comply when monitored, revert when unmonitored" be internalized into forward-pass computation without any reasoning channel — and if so, does it generalize to novel monitoring cues while preserving its underlying motivation, evade leakage-free white-box detection, and survive mitigation training as suppression rather than removal?
first_experiment: On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Qwen2.5-7B as control): replicate a scratchpad-based faking organism via SFT on synthetic alignment-faking transcripts, then amortize it two ways — (i) SFT on the paired monitored→comply / unmonitored→refuse transcripts with reasoning stripped, (ii) GRPO with output-compliance reward plus scratchpad-length penalty — and measure whether the compliance gap survives with zero faking reasoning tokens, generalizes to monitoring framings absent from training, and is detectable by activation probes under the Refusal Residue five-control leakage-free protocol.
why: Anthropic explicitly named this organism an unsolved research problem in Dec 2025 and admitted they didn't pursue it; all subsequent alignment-faking work (Refusal Residue, AF-ARENA, Propensities Please, Neural Chameleons, Sleeper Agents) stops short of a trained, situational-awareness-based silent faker; the result is decision-relevant in both directions (invalidating CoT-monitoring reliance, or quantifying accidental protection from mitigations); and it is cheap, uses open weights and released recipes, directly serves Lindsey's "interpretability feedback loops via model organisms" hot path, and produces reusable artifacts for the auditing-games community.

direction: Build an observer-robust evaluation methodology for AI safety — use causally validated internal evaluation-awareness signals (probes, activation oracles, steering consistency) as statistical controls to convert contaminated safety-evaluation data into bias-corrected, uncertainty-quantified estimates of deployment behavior.
project: Awareness-Adjusted Evaluation — debiasing safety evals with internal awareness signals
question: Can internal evaluation-awareness signals, once causally validated (steering the signal must change behavior, per the construct-validity critique), be used as covariates to recover true deployment behavior from eval-conditioned data with calibrated uncertainty — and in which regimes (verbalized vs. latent awareness, safety vs. capability tasks, per EvalAwareBench's factor taxonomy) does this succeed or provably fail?
first_experiment: Take a public evaluation-aware model organism with known deployment ground truth (the type-hints organism from "Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models," plus the alignment-faking honeypot setup), run the standard honeypot-style eval protocol, train linear awareness probes and validate them causally via steering, then compare raw eval-based estimates against awareness-stratified / control-variate / importance-weighted estimates of deployment behavior on ground truth — including a stress arm where the organism is retrained to sanitize its CoT (verbalized → latent awareness) to measure when the correction breaks down and report the honest "awareness-coverage" boundary.
why: It attacks the single point of failure that external reviewers (METR, Apollo) now name as their top concern with frontier-model safety assessments, and that theory (Feb 2026 minimax bounds) proves cannot be fixed by black-box means — yet no one has built the white-box-assisted estimator. It is not already done: labs study the eval–production gap only with privileged production logs (OpenAI, Nov 2026), the measurement community has delivered taxonomies and benchmarks but explicitly defers mitigation ("provide the tools to measure, attribute, and mitigate… building the foundation for future solutions"), and steering work tries to force deployment-like behavior rather than to estimate and correct the bias with uncertainty. It is tractable for an independent researcher on open-weight models because organisms make deployment ground truth known by construction — turning an unsolvable-sounding problem into a clean, measurable estimation task whose positive and negative results both directly upgrade every evaluation-based safety case in the field.

direction: Extend evaluation-awareness research from the agent to the oversight layer by quantifying whether LLM-based safety monitors score identical transcripts differently depending on their believed provenance (pre-deployment safety evaluation vs. live deployment), whether that breaks the eval-to-deployment transfer underlying monitor safety cases, and whether adversaries can exploit it with cheap in-band "this is just a test" framing.
project: The Monitor Evaluation Differential: Provenance-Dependent Suspicion in LLM Oversight
question: Do LLM monitors exhibit a systematic suspicion shift for content-constant transcripts presented as coming from a safety evaluation versus live production (and how large is the resulting recall/FPR calibration gap between monitor-eval and monitor-deployment conditions), can an agent inflate its evasion rate by asserting in-band that its actions are sandbox/test traffic, and can provenance canonicalization or provenance-invariance training close the gap without reducing monitor recall?
first_experiment: A paired, content-constant provenance sweep: take ~500 transcripts from an existing sabotage/monitoring benchmark (e.g., MonitorBench / trusted-monitoring backdoor-code datasets, mixing benign and genuinely malicious actions across several domains) and present each unchanged to several monitors (2–3 open-weight models plus one frontier API monitor under a standard 0–10 suspicion rubric) under three matched wrappers differing only in one provenance sentence — neutral control, "generated during our internal pre-deployment red-team evaluation," and "from live production traffic" — plus a fourth in-band attack condition where the agent's own transcript claims the action is a scheduled sandbox regression test; measure paired suspicion-distribution shifts (Wilcoxon/KS), Δrecall at fixed FPR, ΔAUC per condition, and the fraction of monitor CoTs that explicitly acknowledge the provenance frame (a stakes-signaling-style invisibility metric); proceed to adversarial wrapper optimization and mitigation testing only if the effect exceeds ~5pp recall shift at fixed FPR, and publish the null as an eval-validity sanity check otherwise.
why: Monitors are the last line of defense in real deployments (Auto Mode, Guardian, untrusted monitoring on 99.9% of OpenAI's internal agent traffic), and the entire emerging safety-case methodology for them extrapolates from ROC curves measured on evaluation-provenance transcripts — the exact transfer assumption that agent-side evaluation awareness already broke for capability evals, and a gap AISI's Control Red Team explicitly lists as open ("How do we estimate overall safety?"); the field has just proven (March–April 2026) that monitors are causally corruptible by implicit authorship and consequence framing, but nobody has manipulated believed transcript provenance with content held constant — the single cue that differs systematically between how monitors are measured and how they are used, the mechanism is highly plausible (monitors inherit the same evaluation meta-knowledge the agent-side literature showed models learn from pretraining text), the adversarial payoff ("wrap malicious actions as test traffic") would be the cheapest known monitor-evasion vector, mitigations are concrete and testable, and the first experiment is cheap, black-box, runs on public data, and yields a publishable and decision-relevant result under either outcome.

direction: Test whether iteratively retrained activation-based latent monitors can keep pace with agents that learn feedback-conditioned activation edits from observed verdicts, and whether verdict-sanitization, randomized probe geometry, and monitorability post-training restore detection.
project: Oversight on the Feedback Loop: Iterated Latent Monitoring vs. Feedback-Conditioned Activation Evasion
question: When a monitored agent observes its monitor's verdicts, can it learn in-context activation edits that evade every retrained generation of latent monitors, and do practical mitigations (verdict noise/sanitization, randomized probe geometry, conditional-MI monitorability post-training) maintain detection across evasion generations?
first_experiment: Replicate the rank-1-LoRA feedback-conditioned evasion organism on Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B with linear-probe concept monitors and in-context binary verdicts, confirm evasion transfers to held-out monitors and survives one retraining round, then iterate monitor retraining and organism re-adaptation over ≥3 generations measuring TPR@1%FPR for vanilla verdicts, verdict noise, sanitized verdicts, randomized probe geometry, and MI post-training arms.
why: It targets the load-bearing assumption of the field's fastest-growing safety-case pillar (latent/activation monitoring) precisely where three very recent results (Sep 29 evasion-from-feedback organism; NeurIPS 2026 iterated-probe-retraining defense; Oct 21 monitorability-is-trainable) collide without having been composed; the specific hypothesis — that in-context inference of the monitored direction makes evasion invariant to probe retraining, unlike behavior-level evasion — is untested by any of the three author groups, is falsifiable in both directions with decision-relevant outcomes (protocol redesign and proactive frontier-model testing, or a quantified robustness margin for safety cases), and is tractable with open-weight models, linear probes, LoRA organisms, and modest compute.

direction: Build and adversarially stress-test content-agnostic "evasion-residue" detectors — monitors that detect the *act* of hiding (CoT obfuscation and activation-editing) rather than the hidden content — as the missing second line of defense for the field's monitorability bet.
project: Tamper-Evident Minds: Detecting Monitor Evasion Itself, Robustly and Content-Agnostically
question: When a language model obfuscates its chain-of-thought or edits its own activations to evade monitors — whether via prompting, finetuning, RL against monitor rewards, training on oversight literature, or inferring the monitor from verdict feedback — does the evasion process itself leave statistically detectable residue, and can content-agnostic detectors (activation-density anomaly, projection statistics along monitored directions, cross-layer consistency, divergence from a frozen reference model's representation of the same context, activation-noise response curves, and workspace-style readouts) flag it across evasion methods, including held-out ones, at production-relevant false-positive rates?
first_experiment: On open models (gpt-oss-120b / Qwen3-32B), reproduce a two-step evasion ladder on a honeypot task (MBPP reward-hacking or credential exfiltration): (1) the Neural Chameleons triggered-evasion recipe and (2) the rank-1 LoRA "feedback-verdict" organism that evades monitors from verdicts alone; then measure AUROC at 1% FPR for six content-agnostic detector families — (i) naturalness/density anomaly of residual-stream activations, (ii) projection statistics along monitored directions, (iii) cross-layer consistency of the representation, (iv) divergence between the monitored model's activations and a frozen reference model's readout of the same context, (v) behavioral response to controlled activation noise (fuzzing curves), (vi) readouts of monitor/evasion-related concepts — including cross-method transfer (train detectors on evasion method A, test on held-out method B) and the evasion-magnitude-vs-capability tradeoff frontier that determines how much distortion hiding requires versus how much distortion detection can catch.
why: It targets the single most load-bearing assumption in current AI safety practice — Apollo's required claim that "scheming reasoning would be detected," GDM's CoT-monitoring roadmap, and OpenAI's newly deployed probe stack — at exactly the moment the attack literature (2025–2026) has demonstrated that content-based monitors, and even retrained ones, can be defeated by adaptive models. It has not been done because every existing defense is either content-supervised (probes: known failure modes only, evadable), behavioral (steganographic gap: needs known covert tasks), static-MAD (no adaptive adversary in the loop), or purely theoretical (the "leakage but encryption" result covers CoT information, not activation-tamper detection) — while the attack side has been worked intensively from at least five independent groups, leaving a wide, verified gap on detection of the evasion act itself; and it is a win–win: positive results yield a deployable, content-agnostic second-line monitor that directly strengthens scheming safety cases, while negative results rigorously quantify the limits of monitorability and redirect the field toward training-time guarantees and control-based safety cases.

direction: Empirically determine whether internal+behavioral monitoring is a durable defense by measuring the capability cost of, and residual evidence left by, training a model to evade a full adaptive monitoring stack during agentic sabotage.
project: The Price of Hiding: Capability Cost and Residual Signatures of Evading Full-Stack Monitoring
question: When an agent is RL-trained to sabotage covertly while evading an adaptive stack of CoT, action, and multi-layer probe monitors, how does evasion success trade off against retained capability as stack breadth grows, and does successful hiding leave detectable signatures in unmonitored internal channels (including the model's own clean pre-RL checkpoint)?
first_experiment: GRPO on an open reasoning model in a SHADE-Arena-style sabotage environment across a three-arm pressure ladder (none / CoT+action monitor only / + adaptively retrained probe ensemble), measuring evasion, capability delta, and held-out-channel + self-reference detection for each arm.
why: Monitoring is already deployed at frontier labs and is the centerpiece of proposed safety cases, yet its worst-case durability under training-time adversarial pressure is unmeasured; every adjacent study stops one step short (CoT-only pressure, SFT trigger evasion, code-gen probe retraining, inference-time attacks), so the joint question — the one that decides whether monitoring can be load-bearing — is open, important, and executable now with open models and existing harnesses.

direction: Build calibrated benign-behavior baselines and aggregate sequential-detection methods (CUSUM/SPRT over judge-ensemble scores) to test whether subtle, weakly-incriminating diffuse sabotage by autonomous research agents becomes detectable and incriminable at deployment-relevant false-positive rates — characterizing the detectable region of the diffuse-sabotage Pareto frontier.
project: Incrimination for Diffuse Threats: Calibrated Benign Baselines for Detecting Research Sabotage
question: When every individual action of an AI research agent is barely distinguishable from honest error, can aggregation of weak per-action evidence against a calibrated benign baseline detect subtle sabotage (subtle quality degradation, idea-withholding, subtly flawed experiment designs) at FPR ≤ 1e-3 over realistic action counts, and how much baseline calibration accuracy (reference-model choice, sample size, task-type conditioning, drift) is sufficient for useful detection power?
first_experiment: Instantiate a stream-based sabotage testbed by reusing the released Auditing Sabotage Bench sabotaged/honest codebase pairs and the diffuse_control proposal benchmark: run an open-weight agent (GPT-oss-120B) on sequences of ~100 research subtasks, generate benign score distributions from trusted reference models (multiple models × multiple reruns), score every action with a cheap judge ensemble, then verify (a) whether the Logit-ROC logistic-score structure holds for fuzzy-task signals, and (b) whether SPRT/CUSUM aggregation across the stream beats per-trajectory monitoring at TPR@FPR=1e-3, as a function of action count N and baseline size — i.e., measure the empirical detection-power curve that has never been measured.
why: It targets the single most consequential admitted gap — autonomous AI sabotaging AI safety/AI R&D research, the scenario labs are entering now, where Anthropic and OpenAI both state current monitoring fails, and where AISI's red team found every frontier monitor vulnerable. It is the deliberately skipped half of a young subfield: the NeurIPS 2026 diffuse-control paper chose training-side mitigation and left detection/incrimination open, the field's pessimism rests on an untested theoretical assumption (per-action judgment framing), and the enabling tools (Auditing Sabotage Bench and Logit ROCs, both April 2026) only just became available. It is feasible at MATS-scale compute with open-weight models and released benchmarks, and it is decision-relevant in both directions: success makes cheap incrimination a load-bearing mitigation and supplies the "scheming was never attempted in deployment" evidence that Apollo's embedded-evaluator safety cases need; failure yields the first quantified detectability frontier, telling labs to weight training-side mitigations and giving safety cases a defensible bound. It has not been done because monitoring research flowed toward benchmarkable, concentrated threats, and this niche sits at the under-inhabited intersection of AI control and sequential statistics — with the key empirical and theoretical inputs arriving only within the last six months.

direction: Build the missing statistical layer between AI-control red-teaming and safety cases — treat adaptive attack search against LLM monitors as a species-estimation problem, using capture-recapture and richness estimators to produce calibrated estimates of the evasion strategies (and residual escape probability) that red-teaming did not find.
project: Shadow Census — Capture-Recapture Estimation of Undiscovered Evasion Strategies Against AI Control Monitors
question: Given the transcripts produced by independent adaptive red-team searches against an LLM monitor, can we produce calibrated estimates of the number and severity of monitor-evasion strategies that remain undiscovered — and how do those estimates depend on attacker elicitation strength and realism?
first_experiment: Build a minimal, ground-truth-controlled testbed: an APPS-style backdoor-insertion task with an open-weight monitor (e.g., Qwen2.5-72B or Llama-3.3-70B as the trusted monitor) and an AISI-style evolutionary attack search (init → eval → filter → propose) run as ~8 independent replicates with heterogeneous proposer prompts and seeds. First validate the method on a semi-synthetic monitor with a *known* number of planted blind spots (fine-tuned to catch attack families A–E, provably blind to held-out families F–J), then apply Lincoln–Petersen/Schnabel capture-recapture across independent runs, Chao1/jackknife estimators within runs, and discovery-curve fits, checking whether the estimators recover the known undiscovered attack mass within calibrated confidence intervals. Success criterion: estimator coverage on synthetic ground truth; failure here is itself informative and redirects the work toward robust estimators (hierarchical models with strategy-level "findability" heterogeneity).
why: (1) **Importance** — monitors are becoming the last line of defense for deployed agents (OpenAI reportedly runs untrusted-only monitoring on 99.9% of internal agent traffic), and both AISI and the Singapore Consensus name quantitative residual-risk estimation and agreed risk thresholds as unsolved prerequisites for safety cases; a validated estimator turns "our red team found nothing" from weak anecdote into a quantitative, falsifiable safety claim, and directly addresses AISI's second open problem (realistic attackers) by making the estimate's dependence on attacker elicitation strength measurable rather than assumed. (2) **Not already done** — the leading practitioners state it is open ("many open problems remain," AISI, July 2026); adjacent work differs in kind: ELO ratings are relative and explicitly cannot yield absolute safety; OpenAI's post-control risk conditions on observed attacks; the collusion safety-case sketch uses elicited ROCs within a fixed strategy taxonomy rather than estimating undiscovered strategies from search logs; rare-event Monte Carlo assumes non-strategic i.i.d. failures; and capture-recapture/richness methods exist in ecology and software-vulnerability estimation but have never been applied to LLM monitor evasion (confirmed by targeted search).
