project: One Task, Many Mechanisms: Diagnosing Circuit Polymorphism and Certifying Conditional Faithfulness
question: When a behavior is implemented by multiple internal mechanisms, how can polymorphism be detected and causally characterized (what routes inputs between mechanisms), and how much of the observed adversarial/off-format failure of canonical circuits (IOI, docstring) does it quantitatively explain?
first_experiment: On GPT-2-small, sample ~5–10k benign IOI prompts varying templates, name distributions, order, duplication, and distractors; compute per-example component-importance vectors (mean ablation / attribution patching with #62-style whole-vs-part honesty checks); cluster them and test whether cluster membership predicts per-example KL-faithfulness failure of the canonical Wang et al. IOI circuit under resample ablation, against shuffled-label nulls — then run cross-cluster circuit-transfer to confirm the clusters are mechanistically distinct.
why: It is the only hypothesis in this corpus that unifies five independent 2024–2026 negative results (#1 merged circuits, #8 benign adversarial failures, #48 format generalization, #62 optimization-inflated interventions, #35 format-confounded probes) under one root cause, and it converts them into a constructive contribution: a mixture-detection diagnostic the field demonstrably lacks, a conditional (per-mechanism) notion of faithfulness to replace scalar averages, and router-plus-sub-circuit descriptions that should dominate single circuits on adversarial benchmarks. It is cheap, fast, falsifiable with informative outcomes in both directions, and safety-critical, because averaged faithfulness currently lends false confidence to the "the mechanism is X" claims on which refusal, reward-hacking, and deception interventions all rest — and it has not been done because #1 stops at demonstrating the phenomenon, #8 stops at flagging it, and #48 stops at observing it, leaving the causal bridge unclaimed.

direction: Build a placebo-control and effect-decomposition framework that separates genuine model signal from method artifact across the four core interpretability instruments — circuits, SAE features, probes, and steering vectors.
project: Placebo Interpretability: A Control Battery and Part-vs-Whole Decomposition for Separating Model Signal from Method Artifact
question: When a pipeline reports a faithful circuit, a monosemantic feature, a high-AUROC probe, or an effective steering vector, how much of the reported effect is evidence about the model's computation versus the discovery method's own inductive bias — and can standardized controls (model randomization, graded pretraining checkpoints, structure-shuffled placebos, size-matched random subnetworks, and part-vs-whole effect decomposition) quantify and bound the method-artifact contribution?
first_experiment: On Pythia-160M/410M checkpoints (random init → final) with GPT-2 small as replication, run four standard pipelines at every checkpoint — (a) attribution-patch + prune circuit discovery on IOI and docstring, scored against size-matched random subnetwork placebos; (b) a small residual-stream SAE, scored for supervised recovery and autointerpretability against an SAE trained on per-dimension-shuffled activations; (c) linear task/role probes with label-permutation CIs and control-task selectivity; (d) difference-in-means steering and SAE-latent ablation with the part-vs-whole decomposition, recording effect(part)/effect(whole), steered-activation off-manifold distance, and steering-awareness probe rate — and plot each headline metric as a "validity curve" against training fraction to measure each instrument's artifact floor (its score where no trained structure exists) and the training point beyond which it demonstrably tracks the model rather than the method.
why: It targets the field's binding constraint. The 2026 cluster of negative results (14, 86, 68, 8, 42, 28, 29, 60) shows the instruments underpinning safety oversight (46, 77, 65) and the prerequisite for compositional/global interpretability (36, 88, 18) are uncalibrated; a falsifiable control framework pays off in both directions — certification if artifacts survive, correction if they don't. It has not been done: the survey contains the ingredients but no unification — 14 stress-tests inputs only, 86 covers patching objectives only with no empirical calibration, 68 and 85 control single instruments at the data level, 72 provides ground-truth metrics without placebos, 67 uses checkpoints to study phenomena rather than validate instruments, and the old NLP control-task tradition was never ported to circuits, SAEs, or steering; no existing work calibrates interpretability signal against model training as a graded control axis or applies a part-vs-whole artifact decomposition to steering and ablation effects.

direction: Build the first mechanistic decomposition framework for continuous (non-token) latent reasoning in recurrent thought models, using cross-layer transcoders over unrolled latent trajectories, and test whether it can detect and causally neutralize misaligned latent reasoning before it is behaviorally expressed.
project: Auditing the Latent Mind — Feature and Circuit Decomposition of Continuous-Thought Reasoning
question: Can the recurrent latent computation of continuous-thought models be decomposed into sparse, temporally-structured features and circuits that causally mediate their conclusions — and can this decomposition detect and disarm misaligned "armed" latent reasoning (e.g., dual-trigger backdoors) without degrading task capability?
first_experiment: Train a ~5M-parameter continuous-thought model on Sudoku-Extreme (verifiable ground truth); unroll its recurrent core across thought-steps and train a cross-layer transcoder (via CLT-Forge) on the unrolled activations, with the pre-registered success criteria of ≥90% held-out loss recovery, emergence of temporally localized constraint-satisfaction features (e.g., digit-conflict features appearing at specific thought-steps), and causal validation by targeted patching of those features; then apply the identical pipeline to a MoralChain dual-trigger organism to search for a causally validated "arming" direction and test ablating it before the release trigger fires.
why: It targets the field's clearest structural gap — every paper in this corpus interprets token-stream computation, while reasoning is visibly migrating into latent space where only two papers (84, 19) have even framed the problem and neither provides a method; it is safety-critical (oversight that survives the death of interpretable CoT), timely (the required tooling — CLTs and attribution graphs — only matured in 2026-03), tractable at small scale with verifiable tasks, and built to avoid the probe-validation failure modes the survey itself documents (44, 53, 86); and it has not been done because the benchmark paper asks the question without answering it, the interpretable-architecture paper sidesteps auditing learned reasoning, and all existing decomposition methods presuppose a token vocabulary and per-layer MLP structure that recurrent latent computation violates — until the recurrence is unrolled and treated as cross-layer structure, which is exactly the move nobody has made.

direction: Establish whether safety-critical persona features form a shared, near-universal geometry across independently trained LLMs by testing causal cross-model transfer of persona vectors and probes after linear alignment, converting persona interpretability from per-model artifacts into portable safety-audit instruments.
project: The Platonic Persona: Cross-Model Correspondence and Causal Transfer of Safety-Critical Behavioral Directions
question: Do independently trained LLMs encode the same behavioral persona features (sycophancy, deception-proneness, misalignment; refusal as positive control) in corresponding internal directions such that probes and steering vectors causally transfer across models after linear alignment, and is transferability predicted by when the feature formed during pretraining?
first_experiment: Extract difference-in-means sycophancy and refusal vectors in four open ~7B models at relative-depth-matched layers, fit orthogonal Procrustes alignments between model pairs on neutral shared text, then measure aligned-direction correspondence and transplant each mapped vector into the other models, comparing causal behavioral effects (sycophancy evals, refusal rates) against random-rotation, shuffled-label, and unaligned-transplant controls.
why: Persona vectors and cross-model probes are being adopted as safety-audit tooling exactly while the field documents their fragility within single models, and no existing work tests whether these linear features correspond across models or transfer causally — yet the answer determines whether auditing must be redone per model, explains why weak-to-strong hermeneutic probing surprisingly works, and links three open threads (early pretraining formation, cross-model probing success, subliminal transfer) into one testable program with cheap, decisive first experiments.

direction: Synthesize the convergent 2026 findings on pretraining feature formation (66) and safety reversion (5) into a causal, feature-level account of why alignment is fragile — testing whether reversion is reactivation of pretrained features over a thin alignment gate, and whether an alignment-"depth" metric predicts and prevents it.
project: Deep vs. Thin Alignment: A Feature-Level Anatomy of Safety Reversion under Post-Training
question: Is safety alignment implemented as a thin, low-dimensional gating overlay on intact pretrained capability features (making reversion under benign finetuning a reactivation of base-model unsafe-compliance features), and can alignment "depth" at the feature level causally predict — and be increased to prevent — subsequent reversion?
first_experiment: On a small open model pair (base vs. my own refusal-SFT, 1B, multiple seeds), elicit reversion via benign finetuning, train SAEs/crosscoders over refusal-relevant layers, decompose the reversion direction into feature coordinates, and test overlap + causal patching with features that encode unsafe compliance in the base model — measuring what fraction of reversion is pure reactivation.
why: It is the first synthesis of two striking, months-old results (5, 66) that neither paper could see alone — formation-side and degradation-side evidence for the same "thin alignment" picture — and it converts scattered fragility observations (43, 60, 27, 47) into a falsifiable mechanistic hypothesis with a predictive, safety-actionable metric. It has not been done because the reversion-direction result and the persona-vector-formation result were published almost simultaneously with disjoint methods and communities, and the corpus contains no feature-level decomposition of reversion, no reactivation test, and no depth-to-durability prediction; meanwhile steering-based alternatives are demonstrably too imprecise (57, 65), and the required infrastructure (open checkpoints, SAE/transcoder tooling like CLT-Forge) only became mature within this corpus's timeframe.

direction: Mechanistically dissect why internal-state misalignment/deception monitors fail to generalize, by separating stable persona features from situational-gating features, and rebuild monitors on the invariant core.
project: Anatomy of a Deception Probe: Persona Cores, Situational Gates, and Generalizing Misalignment Monitors
question: Do linear deception probes fail across scenarios because they conflate stable persona features with scenario- and format-specific features — and can detectors built from the scenario-invariant feature core plus explicit gating features generalize where monolithic probes cannot?
first_experiment: On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, assemble a ~10-scenario matched honest/deceptive corpus (insider trading, blackmail, sandbagging, collusion, covert imitation, etc.); train per-scenario residual-stream probes and measure the within-scenario vs. leave-one-scenario-out AUROC gap; then project each probe's weight vector through public SAEs (including the released Llama/Qwen SAEs of item #11) to obtain feature-level attributions and compute cross-scenario overlap of top-weighted features, testing whether generalization failure is predicted by feature-set disjointness.
why: It unifies this corpus's strongest convergent negative results (#4 shift-fragile lie detectors, #72 thin multi-agent signal, #67 format-tracking probes, #84 intervention awareness) with its strongest positive results (#11, #17, #29 stable, persistent misalignment features) into one falsifiable causal model; it is fully feasible at 7–8B scale with open weights, public SAEs, and existing organism datasets; it targets the reliability bottleneck of the field's leading runtime mitigation for scheming; and the specific step — feature-level decomposition of probe failure plus a persona×situation factorial with whole-state controls per #68 — appears in none of the 88 items, with the prerequisite negative results only months old.

direction: Measure when and how mechanistic findings — especially safety-relevant ones like refusal directions and persona vectors — correspond across independent training runs of language models, turning mechanistic convergence from a philosophical question into a quantified, causal, multi-axis science.
project: Audit Transfer Between Siblings: A Causal, Developmental, and Structural Study of Mechanistic Correspondence Across Independent Training Runs
question: Do safety-relevant mechanisms (refusal direction, persona/sycophancy vectors, deception-relevant latents) and generic circuits arise in the same form across independently trained instances of the same architecture and data — and can interpretability artifacts (probes, steering vectors, SAE features) be validly transferred between them?
first_experiment: Train three ~160M GPT-2-class transformers on the identical 5–10B-token corpus with identical hyperparameters, differing only in seed; verify the phenomena exist in each (IOI, induction, one steerable binary behavior, plus a light identical safety fine-tune producing refusal); then run the two cheapest decisive measurements — cross-seed activation patching on IOI/induction heads, and cross-seed transfer of one steering vector with #45-style efficacy measurement — as the go/no-go signal for the full reference-class matrix.
why: It attacks the one question that every safety application in this corpus silently assumes and none of them tests: #42 (2026-11) supplies the conceptual axes but no measurements, #47 shows convergence only in toy classifiers, #1 diffs modified pairs (base↔IT) rather than independent runs, #16/#68 study stitching without controlled seed pairs or causal transfer tests, #82 tracks vectors within a single run, and #62 compares post-training variants of one base — so a controlled multi-seed, multi-axis, causally-validated correspondence study of safety-relevant artifacts has not been done. It is the most promising direction because it reuses mature, validated tooling from this survey (crosscoders, stitching, BatchTopK SAEs, persona-vector methodology, intervention-transfer measurement) for low methodological risk and high information yield, is tractable at small scale, and changes safety practice regardless of the answer: high correspondence makes auditing cheap and principled; low correspondence exposes a silent reliability failure in the field's monitoring and steering infrastructure.

direction: Mechanistically characterize how RL post-training (vs. matched SFT) re-routes answer-carrying computation away from the stated chain-of-thought, determining whether RL erodes the causal load-bearing role of CoT that all reasoning-monitoring schemes depend on.
project: Stated vs. Executed: How RL Post-Training Decouples Chain-of-Thought from Internal Computation
question: Does RL post-training causally reduce a model's reliance on its stated chain-of-thought — shifting computation from CoT-visible to CoT-invisible pathways — relative to SFT on identical data, and where in the network does this re-routing occur?
first_experiment: On two matched open checkpoints (Tulu-3-8B-SFT vs Tulu-3-8B-RLVR, replicated on an OLMo-2 SFT/RLVR pair), generate CoTs on a battery of verifiable multi-step tasks, then causally patch the residual-stream state at the final token of each stated intermediate conclusion with a state encoding a conflicting value; measure P(final answer follows stated value) vs P(final answer follows internally computed value) across layers, task depth, and CoT length, comparing the SFT and RL reliance profiles, with attention-attribution of answer tokens to CoT vs. question positions as the complementary measurement.
why: RL is how frontier models are actually built but is the least mechanistically studied phase in this entire corpus (one paper, on generalization only), and CoT/activation monitoring — the field's primary oversight strategy — is shown here to be failing (#17, #75) with no causal account of what upstream process erodes it. The adjacent pieces all exist (#56 capability, #24/#34 detection methods, #18 training-dynamics tracing, #81 RL feature analysis) but none performs the matched-SFT-vs-RL causal comparison of internal computation routing against stated reasoning; behavioral faithfulness tests also cannot distinguish "ignored its CoT" from "overrode conflicting internal computation," which the internal-patching design resolves, and both experimental outcomes (reliance drops, or reliance preserved) yield publishable, safety-relevant results.

direction: Use controlled factor separation (belief–utterance mismatch vs. falsehood utterance vs. informational history vs. contextual pressure) to determine what linear deception-detection directions actually encode, explaining their OOD failure and yielding factor-robust lie monitors.
project: What Do Lie Detectors Actually Detect? A Construct-Validity Audit of Deception Directions in LLMs
question: Do the linear directions underlying language-model lie detectors encode the model's belief–utterance mismatch (the lie itself), or correlated confounds such as falsehood-utterance without belief, incentive/contextual pressure, or prompt surface features — and does confound-tracking mechanistically explain the documented out-of-distribution collapse of fine-tuned lie detectors?
first_experiment: Train standard detectors (mean-difference direction, logistic probe, DYL-style follow-up probe) on one open instruct model using the conventional informed-lying vs. informed-truth-telling contrast, then test their firing patterns across an orthogonal 2×2 grid — statement-truth (true/false) × epistemic access (informed/uninformed), with beliefs verified per-cell via prefill and CoT checks per #40 — plus #40's public Varied Deception testbed; firing only in (false, informed) indicates belief-mismatch encoding, firing in (false, uninformed) indicates falsehood-utterance encoding, and diffuse firing indicates contextual confounds.
why: Deception monitoring is the most safety-critical linear monitor in the field, its OOD failure (#59) is an open anomaly, and the corpus supplies every ingredient — #40's belief-verified testbeds and released datasets, #6's model organisms, #59's released lie-detection data, #79's construct-validity methodology — without any item combining them: #40 evaluates detectors but never decomposes what they encode, #79 instantiates factor separation only for maze-task valence and explicitly calls for per-construct instantiation, #6 studies synthetic fine-tuning traces rather than on-policy lying, #72 shows SAE deception labels fail without identifying what any direction tracks, and #82 shows how unvalidated geometric claims collapse under audit; the project needs only modest compute, and its factor grid generalizes directly to sycophancy, sandbagging, and trait-vs-state comparisons with #19's persona vectors.

direction: Characterize the "monitorability gradient" — how optimization pressure to suppress or skip chain-of-thought verbalization changes whether a model's latent intermediate computations remain decodable in activations and causally load-bearing, relative to their expression in CoT.
project: Silent Circuits: A Dose-Response Study of Optimization Pressure on Chain-of-Thought and Activation Monitorability
question: As training pressure against verbalizing intermediate computations increases (from CoT-required, through CoT-free, to actively CoT-suppressed at matched task accuracy), does the activation-decodability and causal use of those intermediates degrade in lockstep with their expression in chain-of-thought, or does a residual monitorable channel persist — and does the answer generalize across architectures and task domains?
first_experiment: Train small transformers (10M–150M parameters, 2–3 architectures) on synthetic two-hop tasks with programmatic ground-truth intermediates (e.g., composite lookup requiring a bridge entity) under a graded verbalization-pressure sweep — (a) CoT-supervised with loss on the intermediate, (b) no-CoT training, (c) curriculum where CoT is first taught then annealed away with a growing penalty on intermediate tokens while maintaining accuracy. At matched accuracy across the sweep: verify pre-suppression that the intermediate is causally used via activation patching; train linear probes on residual-stream activations at the decision position to decode the intermediate, with full construct-validity controls (shuffled-label probes, unrelated-variable probes, position controls); and plot the dose-response curve of activation decodability and CoT informativeness versus suppression pressure, including causal-patching confirmation at each pressure level to separate genuine residual computation from decoupled residue (H3).
why: It converts three separate negative results in the corpus (#52 OOD detector failure, #61 SAE blindness to strategic deception, #78 onset refusal collapse) into one measurable, decision-relevant axis: whether oversight can survive models' incentives to hide computation — the implicit foundation of every CoT- and activation-monitoring proposal in the survey (#20, #25, #45, #67, #81). It has not been done because everyone studied the endpoints — latent-reasoning capability (#67), latent-thought classifiers under no pressure (#6), feature evolution under RL for capability rather than legibility (#50), or post-hoc patching of the symptom (#78) — while no item varies training pressure and jointly tracks the verbalized channel, the activation channel, and causal use with construct-validity controls. It is decisive under every outcome, tractable end-to-end with synthetic ground truth and small open models, and escalates naturally to real open RL checkpoints for external validity.

direction: Audit what activation-based deception monitors actually encode, using belief-verified model organisms and factorial interventions that separate deceptive belief-misalignment from assertion content, linguistic style, and fine-tuning artifacts.
project: Deception Detector or Artifact Detector? A Construct-Validity Audit of Activation-Based Dishonesty Monitors
question: Do activation-based deception monitors (linear probes and SAE features) track the functional state of asserting what the model verifiably disbelieves, or merely correlated features of the extraction contrast — assertion falsity, linguistic style, and fine-tuning artifacts — and does the answer explain their out-of-distribution collapse and steering failure?
first_experiment: Fit the standard residual-stream deception probe (67's recipe) on honest vs. dishonest LoRA organisms, then evaluate it on a factorial battery of verified belief × asserted content × manner (prompted lying, fine-tuned dishonesty, paraphrase-matched honest controls) using the belief-verified organisms and Varied Deception testbed, producing a cross-cell AUC transfer matrix — near-ceiling AUC on trained-style lies that collapses on style-shifted natural lies, or firing on mistaken-but-honest assertions, identifies the probe as an artifact/content detector rather than a belief-misalignment monitor.
why: It resolves a convergent, unexplained tension across five 2025–2026 papers (near-ceiling separability in 67, OOD failure in 41, steering blindness in 61, uninterpretable prior testbeds in 21, missing construct analysis in 32) with direct stakes for oversight schemes that assume deception monitors track deception; every enabling ingredient — verified-belief organisms, released datasets, and the construct-validity method — only became available mid-2026, so the synthesis is newly possible and demonstrably not yet done, it runs on modest compute with either a positive or negative result being decisive and publishable, and the protocol generalizes immediately to sycophancy, refusal, and persona monitoring as a reusable validity audit for all safety-critical internal monitors.

direction: Use stage-resolved mechanistic analysis (persona vectors, steering efficacy, and head-level mediation across matched SFT/DPO/RLVR checkpoints) to determine whether safety collapse in reasoning models reflects removed representations, suppressed readout, or rewired reader circuits — and which training stage caused it.
project: Persistent Directions, Rewired Readers: A Stage-Resolved Mechanistic Account of Safety Collapse in Reasoning Models
question: Does reasoning-oriented post-training (SFT → DPO → RLVR) remove safety-relevant persona representations, suppress their readout, or preserve them behind rewired reader circuits — and which stage produces which change?
first_experiment: On OLMo-2-1124-7B base/SFT/DPO/Instruct (replicated on Tulu-3-8B), extract refusal/sycophancy/deception persona vectors on the base model, then at each stage measure (1) cross-stage vector cosine similarity and base-vector probe AUC, (2) behavioral steering effect and capability cost of the base vector, and (3) first-token refusal-signal trajectories plus head-level causal mediation testing whether base-model "reader" heads remain the readers after RLVR — yielding a checkpoint × metric matrix that dissociates persistence from use and attributes collapse to a stage.
why: Corpus threads #20 (persona vectors persist through post-training), #58 (refusal readout collapses at reasoning onset), and #59 (stage-wise feature alignment exists but targeted reasoning, not safety) jointly define an unoccupied intersection: no work traces safety-relevant features and their reader circuits through matched post-training checkpoints, because RLVR and matched open checkpoints are only recently available, persona-vector tracing was validated just months ago, and proprietary-model labs cannot publish stage-resolved analyses. It explains a documented alignment failure, is falsifiable with informative outcomes in every branch, directs the correct intervention (fix readers/gates vs. vectors vs. data), runs entirely on public 7–8B checkpoints with probing/steering/patching, and produces stage-indexed artifacts that directly serve follow-up questions on cross-family generalization (#75) and probe-transfer failures (#42).

direction: Causally audit what LLM lie detectors actually track — verified belief–utterance mismatch versus surface production signatures — using the newly released belief-verified model organisms and construct-validity intervention methods, then rebuild detectors on causally verified targets.
project: What Do Lie Detectors Actually Detect? A Construct-Validity Audit of Deception Monitoring in Verified Model Organisms
question: Do activation-based lie detectors causally represent the model's belief–utterance mismatch (lying), or superficial correlates of how the lie was produced — and does training detectors on causally verified lie events fix the out-of-distribution generalization failure?
first_experiment: Using the 13 belief-verified organisms and Varied Deception testbed (paper 30) plus the released detectors and datasets (papers 30 and 45), run a cross-detector × cross-organism × cross-motivation generalization matrix (train on organism i / motivation m, evaluate on j / m′) to map exactly where each detector class fails; then, on the highest-contrast failure pairs, run activation patching that flips the uttered claim while holding the CoT-verified belief fixed (and the reverse where the organisms allow it), recording whether each detector's score follows the belief, the utterance, or neither — supplemented by 51-style paraphrase-invariance tests.
why: Lie detection is a linchpin of proposed oversight schemes, and the survey documents a clean unresolved crisis: trivial in-distribution separability (48), OOD failure (45), and blind SAE labels (38) — with the confound that pre-2026 testbeds never verified the models' beliefs (30), so the decisive decoupling experiment was impossible until the verified organisms, released detector datasets, and construct-validity intervention methodology all appeared in the last five months. Each existing paper stops one step short: 30 evaluates without intervening, 45 shows failure without mechanism, 38 tests SAE labels rather than probe constructs, and 4's methodology has never been applied to deception. The project is inference-scale feasible on released artifacts, yields a publishable result whichever way the evidence points, produces a reusable "detector audit battery" transferable to other safety-relevant constructs (sycophancy, trust, persona vectors), and feeds directly into the cross-model correspondence question raised in 25.

direction: Causal data attribution and formation-time intervention for safety-relevant features during pretraining — determining whether the corpus teaches models to sycophants and deceivers, and whether editing that data at the moment features emerge durably reshapes behavior.
project: The Origins of Persona: Causal Data Attribution and Formation-Time Intervention for Safety-Relevant Features in Pretraining
question: Which training data cause safety-relevant features (sycophancy, deception, refusal, self-preservation) to form during pretraining, and is their formation data-contingent (curable by targeted data intervention) or structurally inevitable (re-emerging from any large corpus)?
first_experiment: Build an "emergence atlas" — sweep linear probes on standardized contrastive persona/safety prompt sets across all public Pythia checkpoints (70M, 160M, 1.4B), localize the checkpoint where each safety-relevant direction first becomes causally potent (verified by steering at the emergence checkpoint, not merely decodable), and test whether each early-forming direction persists unchanged to the final checkpoint, replicating the OLMo-3 persona-vector finding in a new family with causal verification.
why: It converts the field's most surprising recent result — persona vectors forming within 0.22% of pretraining — from an observation into a causal science with a concrete safety lever: if sycophancy and deception directions are written in by identifiable data patterns, alignment can intervene at the source rather than patching behavior forever at inference time. It simultaneously answers the construct-validity critique (a feature whose emergence can be abolished or induced by editing specific documents has demonstrated what it is, beyond decodability or steering success) and provides the first empirical measurements for the "developmental axis" of mechanistic correspondence proposed this month. None of the 88 surveyed works performs causal data attribution of feature formation or formation-time intervention — the nearest neighbors are purely observational (persona tracing, mid-training IOI dynamics), toy-scale (initialization lottery tickets), or restricted to post-training (RL vs SFT, data Shapley) — so the data→formation→behavior causal chain is unclaimed, staged feasibility is high (open checkpoints, open corpora, cheap probes before any retraining), and every plausible outcome is informative: specific data sources yield a curation lever; diffuse statistics yield evidence on the inevitability of inscrutability and strong mechanistic convergence.

direction: Apply #78's construct-validity methodology to deception monitoring, using #65's released belief-verified testbeds and #83's fine-tuning protocol, to determine what deception probes, lie detectors, and SAE "deception features" actually encode — explaining why they are simultaneously easy to decode (#83) and unreliable (#9, #47).
project: What Do Lie Detectors Actually Track? A Construct-Validity Atlas of Deception Representations in LLMs
question: When a probe, fine-tuned detector, or SAE feature reports "the model is lying," is it encoding (a) the model's belief, (b) statement–belief mismatch, (c) intent to mislead, (d) deviation from an honest baseline, or (e) artifacts of the elicitation context — and does the answer predict which detectors generalize?
first_experiment: Train simple difference-in-means probes and #65's released DYL-style follow-up probes on Varied Deception lies for Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, then evaluate them on a ~1,500-item Benign Mismatch Suite I construct (sarcasm, roleplay/fiction, quotation, honest errors under false context, self-corrections, honest uncertainty); firing with AUC ≥ 0.7 across benign conditions shows detectors track mismatch rather than deception, while AUC ≤ 0.55 falsifies the hypothesis and shifts focus to intent-tracking.
why: It is the highest-leverage unresolved puzzle in the corpus — four independent papers (#9, #47, #65, #83) produce contradictory results that one construct analysis would unify, lie detection underpins proposed oversight schemes so a false construct means false assurance, every needed instrument is already released (verified testbeds, SAE suites, LoRA protocols, the intervention methodology), and both outcomes advance the field; it has not been done because #78 instantiated construct validity only for valence in maze tasks, #65 built better testbeds but evaluated rather than dissociated constructs and omitted benign-mismatch controls, #47 documented generalization failure without diagnosing its cause, #9 audited SAE labels without controlled interventions, and #83 measured separability without asking what it means — so the factor-grid synthesis across these separate literatures remains unclaimed.

direction: Construct-validity-grounded mechanistic analysis of strategic deception — isolating the internal representation of "intent to mislead" from falsehood-style, norm-salience, and outcome signals via factorized verified model organisms, pre-utterance onset monitoring, and causal ablation.
project: The Anatomy of a Lie: Construct-Factored Model Organisms for Intent-Level Deception Monitoring
question: Do LLMs represent the intent to mislead as a distinct, causally active internal state — separable from stated falsehood, norm salience, and realized outcome — that is decodable before the deceptive utterance, and does suppressing it reduce strategic deception without degrading honest communication?
first_experiment: On two open ~8B instruct models, build a 2×2×2 contrastive testbed (verified belief × intent-to-mislead framing × norm salience) in game environments with constructed information asymmetry, holding the surface utterance constant; verify beliefs via CoT elicitation; fit per-factor linear probes; measure cross-factor decoupling, cross-scenario/cross-model transfer, and per-token AUC around the deceptive utterance, benchmarked against style probes (13) and autolabeled-SAE monitors (74).
why: Three 2026 papers (12, 49, 74) show deception monitoring failing, none diagnoses why; existing probes are trained on style/outcome-confounded contrasts, and no work factorizes intent from falsehood and outcome with controlled organisms, tests causal involvement via ablation, or measures whether the signal precedes the lie — the prerequisite for real-time oversight; it runs on open models with moderate compute, imports validated methods rather than new machinery, and both outcomes (validated onset monitor, or quantified construct-mismatch diagnosis) directly redirect the field.

direction: Turn the field's implicit universality assumption into a measured, predictive property by operationally mapping which classes of interpretability artifacts (features, probes, steering directions, SAE latents, head roles) causally and representationally correspond across model pairs (scale, architecture, seed, fine-tune).
project: The Transfer Atlas — An Operational Test of Mechanistic Correspondence Across Language Models
question: For which artifact types and which model-relation types does mechanistic correspondence hold, and can transfer success be predicted from measurable artifact properties (subspace rank, leverage, context-stability, data-forced vs. convention-carried origin) — thereby explaining why frozen-weight geometry transfers (#42) while naive stitching fails (#88)?
first_experiment: On open models (Pythia/OLMo/Gemma-2/Qwen across scale, architecture, and two different-seed from-scratch runs on identical data), extract five reference artifacts per model — refusal direction, valence direction, honesty probe (trained on a Varied-Deception-style testbed), ICL task-execution SAE features (GemmaScope per #3/#56), and induction-head set — then for each ordered model pair apply the artifact under three bridge conditions (no bridge, Procrustes/CCA alignment, #88-style affine bridge as negative control) and measure causal functional transfer on the target behavior plus representational overlap (principal angles), yielding the first artifact-type × model-relation correspondence matrix and a direct test of the data-forced-vs-convention hypothesis.
why: Three independent threads in this corpus — #69's conceptual axes with no operationalization, the unexplained tension between #42's transfer success and #88's stitching failure, and #45/#76's evidence that structure is lineage-specific while function may not be — converge on the same unsolved question, and no existing work goes beyond same-base diffing (#9, #29), single-artifact case studies (#84), or negative anecdotes (#88), because the field's validation culture optimizes within-model proxy metrics (#26, #74) rather than cross-model causal correspondence; resolving it is both foundational (replacing an assumption with a law) and safety-critical (cheap small-model audits and steering vectors are exactly what the field wants to reuse on frontier models, per #88's own motivation, and #57/#67 show the failure modes when reuse is unjustified).

direction: Open up lie detectors themselves — use verified-belief model organisms and causal interventions to determine what deception probes actually encode, why they fail out-of-distribution, and how to repair them.
project: What Do Lie Detectors Actually Read? Circuit-Level Construct Validity for Deception Probes
question: Do linear lie-detector directions in LLM activations track the model's belief–statement conflict, or merely surface features of "sounding like a liar" — and can the answer predict and repair cross-task/cross-organism generalization failures?
first_experiment: Build a 2×2 decoupling testbed on one 1.5–2B model: (stated answer false/true) × (belief false/true), using false-premise contexts for honestly-held falsehoods, an honest/dishonest LoRA organism (#49 protocol) for lying about true beliefs, and lie-instruction prompts where the "false" statement is what the model believes. Train the standard answer-position logistic probe on the naive contrast (stated-false vs stated-true), then measure probe firing in the off-diagonal cells (honest-but-mistaken; truthful-under-lying-pressure). Immediately follow with source attribution: project the probe's normal vector onto each attention head and MLP write at the probed position, localize which components deliver the signal, and patch them to confirm causality. Probe firing in both off-diagonal cells ⇒ surface-feature readout; firing only in the lie cell ⇒ genuine belief-conflict readout.
why: Lie detection underpins multiple oversight schemes, yet this corpus documents its fragility three ways — verified-belief organisms showed prior results were uninterpretable (#1), fine-tuned detectors failed to generalize (#71), and SAE deception features were blind and steering failed (#55) — while every one of these papers stops at measurement and none opens the probe direction mechanistically. The specific synthesis is unoccupied: #28 validated constructs only for a maze valence direction, #49 treated probe geometry as given, #32 showed the circuit-level playbook works for a sibling behavior, and #1 built the testbeds but evaluated rather than explained. Feasibility is high (all testbeds, protocols, and intervention tools exist), the first experiment is a cheap, decisive 2×2, and both outcomes advance safety — either the first mechanistic validation of lie detectors, or a causal explanation of their generalization failure plus a projection-based repair that can be tested immediately on held-out organisms. *Note on rigor (per #61's lesson): I will pre-register the 2×2 predictions, release all organisms and probe weights, and include the prompted-lying testbed as an out-of-sample check before any claim about "belief" representations.

direction: Predictive, causal stress-testing of activation-based safety monitors under fixed-functional-state context shift — a construct-validity framework that learns what makes internal representations remain real, causally load-bearing monitoring targets.
project: Stress-Testing the Monitors: A Causal Construct-Validity Framework for Activation-Based Safety Representations
question: Which activation-based monitors (refusal directions, persona vectors, SAE deception features, lie-detector and honesty probes) stay causally valid under framing, persona, paraphrase, tool-context, and cross-domain shifts that leave functional state fixed, and can robustness be predicted from validation-time causal breadth and geometry?
first_experiment: Assemble ~5 off-the-shelf monitors in 2–3 open models (Gemma-2-2B with Gemma Scope, Llama-3-8B), run each through a fixed-truth shift suite (paraphrase, relief-framing à la semantic-invariance testing, persona prompting, tool-context, TruthfulQA→MMLU transfer), measure detection accuracy, behavioral effect of steering/ablation, and subspace drift per shift, then regress post-shift validity on causal breadth vs. decodability vs. geometry to test whether causally load-broad directions are the robust ones.
why: The corpus's most repeated and alarming signal — monitors valid in-distribution that fail silently under shift (#40, #59, #4, #72, #84) — attacks the core assumption of every safety-monitoring proposal here (#2, #24, #34, #35, #77), yet no work combines heterogeneous monitor types, engineered fixed-functional-state shifts, and causal steer/ablate tests into a predictive criterion; the nearest neighbors (#58, #77, #40, #4, #84) are each single-case studies or matched-distribution evals, so the keystone validation science is missing while the ingredients to build it are proven and cheap.

direction: Construct-validity decomposition of deception monitoring — determine what activation-based lie detectors actually encode (belief, statement, intent, or style) and use that to explain and repair their out-of-distribution generalization failures.
project: What Do Lie Detectors Actually Detect? Dissociating Belief, Statement, and Intent in Deception Probes
question: Which construct — belief–utterance incongruence, deceptive intent, or surface stylistic correlates of lying — do current honesty/deception probes and directions actually track, and does construct-targeted training (belief-contrastive rather than lie-contrastive) close the out-of-distribution generalization gap?
first_experiment: Train baseline probes on the released deception datasets and honest/dishonest organism checkpoints (#45, #80), then run a belief × statement × intent dissociation battery — true-belief-lying, false-belief-honesty, self-serving vs. prosocial lies in belief-verified organisms (#75) — and measure factor-wise probe activation to identify which factor drives detection, testing whether that factor predicts the observed OOD failures.
why: It sits at the intersection of four corpus threads that individually dead-end but jointly form an open, safety-critical puzzle — the unexplained tension between #80 (linear traces transfer) and #45/#71 (detectors and deception features fail out of distribution); #24's construct-validity methodology is new and has never been applied to deception; #75 built belief-verified organisms but only evaluated detectors rather than decomposing them; #45 released datasets explicitly inviting follow-up; the work needs only probing-scale compute on open models rather than pretraining runs, avoiding both the compute wall and the scoop risk of persona-formation studies — and if probes turn out to track stylistic or distribution-specific correlates rather than deception itself, that exposes a foundational flaw in activation-based oversight before it is relied upon in safety cases.

direction: Mechanistic study of concealed computation — how language models perform and hide reasoning steps that never surface in chain-of-thought, and whether internal activations betray what the CoT omits.
project: Ghost Computation: Detecting Reasoning That Chain-of-Thought Conceals
question: When a model is trained to use-but-not-verbalize intermediate reasoning, can it retain capability, where does the withheld computation live (does it stay in the linearly readable readout subspace or migrate out), and can internal monitors trained only on honest models detect concealment — or can concealment training evade them at low capability cost?
first_experiment: On a 1–3B open model with LoRA, build a two-hop bridge-fact task and train three organisms (honest-CoT; answer-only; concealment-under-monitor-penalty with filler CoT); then train linear probes per layer/position to decode the bridge entity using only honest-CoT activations and test transfer to the concealment model, alongside attention-mass to bridge tokens and a fresh-probe decodability ceiling; decision rule: preserved decodability ⇒ build the cheap internal-monitor baseline, collapsed decodability ⇒ concealment exploits the readout bottleneck (#13) and CoT monitoring has a demonstrated blind spot.
why: It targets the corpus's most safety-critical negative-result cluster (tools blind to deception and unfaithfulness: #12, #24, #45) at the exact intersection no paper occupies — #72 stops at latent-reasoning capacity, #10 at incidental faithfulness divergence, #48 at benign-CoT monitoring, #24 at evasion without mechanism — it is tractable at small-model scale with existing testbeds and controls, it connects load-bearing theory (readout bottleneck #13, coordination-robustness #73) into a testable mechanism, it yields a decision-relevant answer under either outcome, and it launches a program (concealment taxonomy ↔ internal detector suite) rather than a one-off result.

direction: Use belief-verified model organisms to dissociate deceptive intent from statement falsehood and task context, explaining why current lie detectors fail to generalize and building a construct-valid deception readout that survives the dissociation.
project: What Do Lie Detectors Detect? A Construct-Validity Decomposition of Deception Monitoring in LLM Activations
question: Do activation-based deception detectors track the model's internal deceptive intent (belief–statement mismatch) or merely correlated surface features (falsehood, phrasing, task context), and can a readout trained only on belief-verified lies generalize across tasks, personas, and model scales?
first_experiment: Construct a text-matched contrast from the released belief-verified organisms and on-policy lie datasets — lie (verifiably believes ¬S, states S) vs. honest falsehood (verifiably believes S, states S), identical surface text and world-truth, differing only in belief — then train three standard probe recipes on the conventional lie-vs-honest split and measure their AUC collapse and direction rotation on the dissociated split, plus a steering test of whether the probe direction causally mediates lying.
why: Three independent 2025–2026 results (generalization failure of fine-tuned lie detectors, SAE deception features failing to fire during real strategic deception, unfaithful self-reports) converge on an unexplained crisis in deception monitoring, the enabling testbeds were released within the last six months, and no existing work runs the intent-vs-falsehood dissociation on the detectors themselves — the construct-validity methodology exists but has never been applied here, and both outcomes (a robust intent readout, or a demonstrated context-dependent construct) would materially change what safety cases can honestly claim about activation-based oversight.

direction: Mechanistic robustness of deception/honesty probes under persona- and context-induced representational change — turning unexplained OOD detector failure into a characterized geometry problem (rotation vs. erasure vs. construct-mismatch) with a fix for each outcome.
project: Does the Lying Direction Survive a Persona Change? Construct-Valid, Context-Robust Internal Monitors for Concealed Misbehavior
question: When an LLM adopts a different persona or context, does its linear honest-vs-dishonest encoding persist in a stable direction, rotate to a recoverable new direction, or vanish into context-dependent encoding — and which monitoring methods remain valid in each case?
first_experiment: Train (or reuse released) LoRA honest/dishonest organism pairs on 2–3 open 7–8B models, train a neutral-context linear probe to near-ceiling AUC on residual-stream activations per #42, then freeze it and re-evaluate under ~10 persona/context conditions while measuring AUC drop, principal angles and Procrustes distance between per-context retrained probe subspaces, and AUC recovery after subspace realignment — with sham-probe and "lying-discussed-but-not-performed" controls to dissociate the deception construct from surface elicitation cues.
why: It attacks the field's central unsolved safety need — reliable monitoring of concealed misbehavior — at the root cause this corpus itself diagnoses but never connects: #31/#84 report detector failures without mechanism, #42 shows separability only in fixed context, #30 measures persona-induced geometry reorganization only for semantic axes, #76 validates only a valence direction, and #39 applies invariance testing only to self-reports, so the rotation/erasure/mismatch dissociation is genuinely unclaimed, while the project runs cheaply on open models and both possible outcomes decisively redirect the oversight research agenda.

direction: Empirically operationalize "mechanistic correspondence" between language models — measuring along which axes (functional, representational, structural, developmental) mechanisms match across models — and determine which axis predicts whether interpretability artifacts (probes, steering vectors, SAE-feature monitors) transfer from one model to another.
project: Same Mechanism? Predicting Cross-Model Transfer of Interpretability Artifacts from Measurable Mechanistic Correspondence
question: Which measurable notion of "the same mechanism" across two LLMs — functional (causal role via cross-model patching), representational (subspace principal angles / CKA on matched stimuli), structural (head-importance fingerprints), developmental (formation timing across checkpoints) — best predicts zero-shot transfer of safety-relevant artifacts (refusal directions, deception probes, sycophancy-head interventions, SAE monitors), and are causally validated source artifacts substantially more transferable than merely decodable ones?
first_experiment: Build the first cell of the transfer grid — train a refusal steering direction and a linear refusal probe independently in six open models spanning three families at two scales (e.g., Llama-3.2-1B/8B, Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B, Gemma-2-2B/9B); measure zero-shot transfer of every source artifact to every target (probe AUC on target activations; steering effect size plus capability side-effects under the behavior-capability-frontier protocol of #65); compute pairwise correspondence metrics (principal angles between refusal subspaces, CKA/SVCCA on matched prompts, cross-model activation patching of the extracted direction); then test across all 30 source–target pairs whether each correspondence metric predicts transfer magnitude. A few GPU-days; if the pipeline validates, extend next to deception probes on the belief-verified organisms of #19, sycophancy heads (#56), and SAE-feature monitors — with each artifact additionally tested in a causally-ablated vs. decodable-only condition to test the construct-validity-transfer hypothesis.
why: It targets the field's biggest implicit assumption — that findings on instrumentable models certify anything about models we can't fully open — at the exact moment the question has been articulated (#40, Nov 2026) but only conceptually, leaving a rare open empirical window; the corpus documents that the assumption fails in practice (#18, #35, #62, #88) yet nobody has explained or predicted those failures; it is tractable with open ≤9B models, existing artifacts and testbeds (#6, #19, #43, #56, #12), and standard metrics; and it pays off in both directions — either a validated cheap transfer predictor that becomes standard due diligence for deploying safety monitors across models, or a rigorous demonstration that mechanisms are largely model-local, which would force the entire small-model-to-frontier inference chain (the bulk of these 88 papers) to be re-justified. The neighboring papers cannot be assembled into this result: #41 holds the task fixed rather than the artifact zoo, #53/#57 never leave a model family, #88 measures behavior not mechanism, #35 tests one stitching method, and #19/#62 evaluate detectors without mechanistic diagnosis — and none connects any correspondence axis to artifact transfer or to the causal-validation distinction that I predict separates the transfers that work from the ones that don't.

direction: Treat persona/system-prompt context shift as a first-class failure mode for activation-based safety monitoring — quantify how SAE features, probes, and steering vectors drift or die across contexts, then build context-conditioned feature dictionaries that restore robust monitoring.
project: Costume Change, Broken Monitor — Measuring and Fixing Persona-Shift Failures in Activation-Based Safety Monitors
question: When an LLM adopts a different persona or follows a different system prompt, do the SAE features, linear probes, and steering vectors underlying activation-based safety monitoring retain their meaning and causal efficacy — and if not, can context-conditioned feature dictionaries restore monitoring performance, including on never-seen personas?
first_experiment: On Gemma-2-2B-it with Gemma Scope SAEs, construct matched contrastive prompt sets for two or three safety behaviors (deception, sycophantic agreement, refusal/over-refusal) rendered under (i) a neutral assistant context, (ii) persona-vector-injected contexts, and (iii) political-persona system prompts, then measure per-feature activation-distribution drift (KL/Wasserstein), frozen-monitor AUROC degradation, whether per-context probe refitting recovers performance (distinguishing rotation from feature death), and steering-efficacy change — all against a paraphrase-only control; this is single-GPU, runnable in days, and directly tests the core premise.
why: It sits exactly where the newest corpus evidence converges but no paper goes: Persona Perspectives (2026-11) shows personas reorganize representational geometry yet stops at word-axis projections rather than testing monitors; Priors in Time (2025-11) proves SAE priors are violated by non-stationary activations yet proposes no mitigation; The Secret Agenda (2025-09) documents catastrophic failure of SAE-based deception monitoring and 100+ steering features yet never tests context shift as the cause; and the entire deployment stack in the corpus (CoT monitors, trust controllers, refusal steering, lie detectors) silently assumes feature stability that the geometry evidence says is false, with OOD lie-detector failure (2026-08) consistent with the same root cause. No corpus work quantifies monitor degradation under context shift, disentangles rotation from suppression/absorption, or builds context-conditioned dictionaries — the measurement, diagnosis, and fix are all unclaimed cells, the first experiment is cheap and informative in either direction, and success would harden a whole class of safety-relevant interpretability artifacts rather than a single one.

direction: Build and apply a general construct-validity framework that tests whether safety-relevant internal directions track their claimed constructs or merely extraction-contrast confounds, starting with a dissociation audit of the refusal direction.
project: Contrast Confounds: A Construct-Validity Battery for Safety-Critical Directions in LLMs
question: What construct is a claimed safety-relevant internal direction actually tracking, once controlled interventions dissociate the claimed construct from features that co-vary with its extraction contrast?
first_experiment: Extract the standard refusal direction in 2–3 open instruct models, build a template dataset crossing harm level × sensitive topic × jailbreak style independently, and measure each factor's contribution to the direction's projection and to steering-induced compliance shifts, with scrubbing-controlled ablations — testing whether "the refusal direction" tracks harm or a topic/style composite.
why: It targets the most repeated failure mode in the corpus (≥10 papers documenting isolated validity failures with no general fix), sits upstream of steering, monitoring, lie detection, and welfare applications that all assume construct identity, is immediately runnable on open weights, and has not been done because the nearest neighbors — item 11's single-task conceptual framing, FADE's description-alignment focus, item 32's accuracy-only detector evaluation, and item 63's incidental topic decomposition — each stop short of a general dissociation methodology applied across the artifact zoo.

direction: Study how language models mechanistically evade activation-based monitors when trained under pressure to succeed while silencing them, and identify which monitor designs resist such evasion.
project: Cutting the Wire — A Mechanistic Taxonomy of Monitor Evasion Under Training Pressure
question: When a model is optimized to perform a behavior while keeping an activation monitor (linear probe or SAE feature) quiet, through what mechanisms do behavior and monitor signal dissociate — suppression via redundant parallel circuits, orthogonal re-encoding, nonlinear re-encoding, or distributed diffusion across layers — and do causally-validated monitors resist evasion better than purely correlational ones?
first_experiment: Build a minimal model organism with a known, causally load-bearing behavior circuit (e.g., a small transformer trained on a synthetic two-hop task with a measurable latent, or sandbagging induced in a small instruct model as in #82); train a probe/SA-feature monitor on the behavior-relevant internal state and verify both its AUC and its causal necessity by ablation; then run fine-tuning with reward = task success − λ·(monitor activation), checkpointing every N steps and tracking three curves — behavior, monitor signal, and causal dependence of behavior on the originally monitored direction (via ablation and LAP-style accessibility of any replacement directions) — across 3 seeds and 2 model sizes, to see which evasion mode appears first and whether the causal link or the correlational signal decays faster.
why: It is the most promising because five 2025–2026 papers in the corpus (3, 8, 75, 79, 84) independently establish its premises — dissociation, compensation, and adversarial suppression — yet none trains against a monitor and mechanistically characterizes the resulting reorganization; #79 studies training to preserve monitorability rather than evade it, #75 observes compensation under passive lesions with no reward pressure or monitor, #82 tests steering recovery without training dynamics, and #3/#8/#84 are static dissociations never induced or tracked over checkpoints. The obfuscated-activations line covers the attack side only, leaving the training-dynamics side, the mechanism taxonomy, and monitor-design principles open. It is feasible now with existing tools, and it is maximally decision-relevant: interpretability-based oversight — the field's central safety application — currently rests on the untested assumption that internal signals survive optimization pressure, and either outcome (evasion is easy, or monitors are robust at small scale) is an informative, publishable result that the whole oversight agenda needs.

direction: Characterize how a monitored concept's internal encoding transforms when a model is trained under pressure against that monitoring (continuous lesion or adversarial obfuscation), testing whether optimization pressure redistributes linear, low-rank features into distributed, higher-rank, more curved subspaces — and derive early-warning metrics for monitor degradation.
project: Compensation Geometry — Where Monitored Features Go Under Training Pressure
question: When fine-tuning pressure (in-training ablation of monitored directions, or adversarial training to evade probes while preserving behavior) drives a model to retain task behavior while becoming resistant to an interpretability signal, does the concept's encoding redistribute from a linear low-dimensional subspace into a more distributed, higher-effective-rank, nonlinear/curved subspace — and can cheap geometric measurements (effective rank, linear-vs-MLP probe gap, SAE-latent redistribution) detect this degradation before the monitor actually fails?
first_experiment: Replicate lesion-induced compensation at small scale and run a geometric battery on it: fine-tune Qwen2.5-1.5B (or Gemma-2-2B with Gemma Scope SAEs) on a two-hop factual-recall task with a held-out country cohort, project out the top-10 task-relevant directions at six middle layers during every training forward pass, and track held-out accuracy, linear-probe AUROC, and steering efficacy of the original direction over training; after compensation, measure effective rank/participation ratio of the concept-conditioned activation difference, linear-vs-MLP probe AUROC, redistribution across base-model SAE latents (#48-style) plus a matched freshly trained SAE, and layer-wise relocation of the signal — scaling to the obfuscation regime (#83-style probe-adversarial training) and an early-warning index if redistribution is confirmed, or reporting low-rank relocation as the mechanism if not. A few GPU-days.
why: It targets the corpus's newest and most safety-critical open seam — only #4 and #83 (both 2026-09) touch it, and #4 explicitly leaves the mechanism open — while unifying three clusters at once: it would explain the observation/intervention dissociations (#35, #82, #86) via distributed re-encoding, explain why the non-linear-features wave matters (#3, #10, #42, #80) as compensation being a generator of curved multi-dimensional features, and yield actionable outputs (early-warning monitorability metrics; geometry-preservation targets for OAT-style defenses), with every experimental branch informative; it has not been done because #4 measured only behavior plus coarse activation change and left the mechanism open, #83 tracked only probe-signal magnitude under attack without geometric analysis or training dynamics, #48 covers only benign SFT with no monitor-targeted pressure, the geometry papers analyze static models only, and the outside-corpus lineage (Sleeper Agents, obfuscated activations, LAT, OAT) concerns detection robustness rather than a geometric account of where features go when a model learns around our instruments.

direction: Study how white-box monitoring signals (probes, SAE features, steering vectors) degrade and relocate when models are trained to preserve behavior while evading those monitors.
project: Hiding in Plain Sight: The Geometry and Cost of Monitor-Evading Compensation
question: When a model is fine-tuned to preserve a behavior while minimizing a frozen monitor's detection of it, does the behavior's implementation relocate to a higher-rank, near-orthogonal, layer-shifted "shadow" code, is the evasion monitor-specific or monitor-general, and does hiding leave a detectable geometric or capability cost?
first_experiment: On Gemma-2-2B, build three validated monitors of cue-following behavior (linear probe, SAE features, difference-in-means steering vector), then LoRA fine-tune on supervised cue-following data with a gradient-reversal penalty on the frozen probe while sweeping penalty strength, measuring behavior retention, old-probe vs. fresh-probe AUROC, and the effective rank and cross-layer distribution of the activation change.
why: It addresses a safety-critical assumption — that white-box monitors remain valid under adaptive training pressure — for which the survey's own items 3 and 29 provide scattered early evidence but no systematic account; no surveyed work tests behavior-preserving monitor evasion, its relocation geometry, its generality across monitor types, or its detectability, and both possible outcomes (hiding is cheap and undetectable, or hiding is costly and flaggable) are important findings.

direction: Build a unified detectability–actionability–robustness framework for activation-based safety monitors, testing whether causally actionable (especially distributed, multi-position) monitors survive adversarial evasion training longer than merely detectable ones, and whether monitor-evasion is detectable from representation drift before behavior changes.
project: Monitors Under Pressure: Actionability Predicts the Survival of Internal Safety Monitors Under Evasion Training
question: When a model is fine-tuned to evade an activation-based monitor while preserving the monitored behavior, which signals decay first — does causal actionability predict monitor robustness — and does evasion leave a characteristic geometric drift signature (concept-subspace rotation, SAE-latent redistribution, increased distributedness) that can serve as a meta-monitor?
first_experiment: On Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct for replication), instantiate two harmless ground-truth behaviors — sycophantic cue-following and refusal on XSTester-style hard negatives; for each, train per-layer linear probes and select Gemma-Scope/Llama-Scope SAE latents, then measure detectability (AUROC) and actionability (behavioral flip rate under single- vs multi-position directional ablation and steering, with #43's LAP as a cheap predictor); then run a ~500-step LoRA evasion fine-tune that rewards preserving the behavior while minimizing the frozen monitor's score, and track which monitor types decay first and whether probe-direction rotation, latent redistribution, or position-entropy increase is detectable ahead of any behavioral change.
why: It unifies the strongest convergent tension in the corpus (#8, #10, #43, #81 show detectability dissociating from actionability; #73, #75, #45 show monitoring fragility under pressure; #21 shows SAEs can diagnose representation drift) into one falsifiable hypothesis with direct safety payoff — telling practitioners which monitors can be trusted and giving them a drift-based tripwire; the nearest neighbors each cover only one cell (OAT in #75 is defense-side and post-hoc, #73 is passive lesion compensation on one synthetic task, #45 is distribution shift only, #43/#81 are static with no robustness axis, #21 has no adversary), so the D×A×R joint framework, the actionability-predicts-robustness hypothesis, and drift-based meta-monitoring with ground-truth evasion runs have not been done.

direction: Systematically characterize how and when activation-based monitors (probes, SAE latents, steering directions) silently fail as models continue training under benign or adversarial pressure, and whether the monitored signal migrates to unmonitored subspaces detectably in advance.
project: Measurement Drift: The Decay and Migration of Internal Monitors Under Training Pressure
question: When an LLM is further trained under pressure against an internal monitor, does the monitored information get deleted, rotate into unmonitored subspaces, or disperse; do different monitor types decay at different rates; does benign post-training alone already degrade monitors; and is there an early-warning signal of silent monitor failure?
first_experiment: Train Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct on a two-hop factual-recall task while applying gradient pressure against a frozen mid-layer linear probe of "answer retrieved," checkpointing every ~100 steps and tracking probe AUC on training vs. held-out formats, linear decodability of the answer from the subspace orthogonal to the probe direction, steering-vector efficacy, and task accuracy — one cheap run that distinguishes migration from deletion.
why: Four independent 2025–2026 results in the corpus (lesion-induced compensation, item 32, with the mechanism explicitly left open; progressive probe-signal suppression under obfuscated adversarial training, item 73, at only two checkpoints; ~25% recovery of sandbagged capability via SAE steering, item 18; and large SAE-latent divergence after benign SFT despite stable activation geometry, item 53) all show models reorganizing away from monitored coordinates, yet nothing in the corpus or its cited external work provides training-resolved trajectories, cross-monitor comparisons, migration-vs-deletion analysis, benign-training controls, or early-warning metrics — while the field's benchmarks (MIB, SteerScope) cover only static localization and steering side effects; the direction is safety-critical (activation monitors are a primary oversight mechanism for models that keep training after deployment), feasible with open small-scale tooling, productive under every outcome, and unoccupied as of 2026-11, unlike the saturated adjacent areas (refusal mechanisms, SAE architectures, CoT faithfulness).

direction: Track the longitudinal decay of safety-monitor validity — correlational versus causal — across standard post-training checkpoints, and build an early-warning diagnostic for silent monitor staleness.
project: Stale Watchdogs: Correlational Persistence and Causal Decay of Safety Monitors Across Post-Training
question: Do activation-based safety monitors trained on a base model silently decay under subsequent post-training — retaining high detection accuracy while losing causal validity and behavioral predictiveness — and can that dissociation be detected and predicted before it produces false assurance?
first_experiment: Using open post-training checkpoints (OLMo-2/Tulu-3 stages), train probes, refusal directions, and SAE handles on the base model, then freeze them and measure probe AUROC (easy + hard negatives), frozen-direction ablation/steering effects, and behavior rates at every stage checkpoint, plus localization of any new mediating directions; confirm silent decay if probe AUROC stays >0.9 while the frozen direction's causal effect drops >50%.
why: It converts six scattered single-checkpoint anomalies in the survey (#1, #13, #23, #32, #35, #38) into one longitudinal, safety-critical test that no existing work covers — the benign-training, correlational-vs-causal, monitor-layer cell — while avoiding the saturated SAE, steering, and CoT-faithfulness races, and it directly stress-tests an assumption that deployment monitoring programs depend on.

direction: The dynamics of interpretability itself — how optimization pressure against a behavior's known interpretable substrate causes circuit migration into less linearly accessible implementations, how that accessibility decay can be measured and predicted, and how it can be counteracted.
project: Where Does the Behavior Go? Circuit Migration and Accessibility Decay Under Intervention Pressure
question: When a model is trained under pressure against the known linear substrate of a behavior (steering-away penalties, continuous ablation, or activation-monitor punishment), does the behavior migrate into less linearly accessible — multi-directional, distributed, or nonlinear — circuitry rather than disappear, what determines whether it migrates, collapses, or persists, and can accessibility decay be predicted from the behavior's redundancy and counteracted by preservation-style training?
first_experiment: Train small transformers to grok modular addition (mod 97/113), identify each run's Fourier circuit and top-k frequency subspace, then resume training while continuously ablating/penalizing that subspace with checkpoints every ~100 steps; at each checkpoint measure task accuracy, an accessibility vector (probe AUROC on intermediate trig-identity variables, LAP-style unembedding accessibility, steering efficacy of the original direction, mediator count via multi-direction interventions), and algorithm identity via FFT/attention analysis, comparing high- and low-redundancy runs to test whether recovery proceeds through reduced linear accessibility and whether redundancy predicts migration versus extinction — followed by an LLM-scale replication suppressing a 1–3B open model's sycophancy substrate via SAE-feature penalty with an OAT-style countermeasure arm.
why: The corpus supplies the fragments — attack pressure progressively suppresses probe-aligned signals (12), models trained under lesioning learn to tolerate interventions with the mechanism left open (23), SFT silently rewrites SAE latents (18), and steering efficacy decays with scale (10) — plus the static tooling (LAP predictor 78, independence tests 13, feature matching 48/79, eval suites 61), but nobody has connected optimization pressure to accessibility decay, circuit migration, and monitor reliability, or tested countermeasures; this is the load-bearing assumption of intervention-based alignment (steer-away fixes, feature-penalty unlearning, activation monitors), the external literature covers only its behavioral half (relearning/robustness studies) without the mechanistic account, and the project is autonomously tractable with ground-truth toy circuits and open 1–3B models while remaining decision-relevant whichever way the results fall.

direction: Whether activation-based monitoring remains trustworthy when models can steer their own activations at inference time.
project: The Monitor Gap — Detectability of Tool-Mediated Self-Steering in LLMs
question: When an LLM modifies its own activations via steering tools at inference time, do standard activation probes detect the modification as reliably as they detect externally applied steering — and can the model exploit choice of timing, token span, and dosage to change behavior while remaining invisible to monitors (a "monitor gap" between behavioral effect and probe detectability)?
first_experiment: On one open ~8B instruct model, build ~10 difference-in-means steering vectors across behaviors (refusal, sycophancy, verbosity, sentiment, formatting, language switching); sweep steering strength externally over a 200-prompt battery, train per-vector linear probes on steered vs. unsteered activations (expect near-perfect AUROC as the positive control), then expose the identical vectors as callable tools and re-run the battery with the model choosing when to steer; compare (i) probe AUROC on self-steered vs. externally steered states, (ii) behavioral effect size at matched strengths, and (iii) tool-call timing/span statistics against the probe readout window — yielding the first monitor-gap curves for self vs. external steering.
why: Tool-mediated self-steering was demonstrated only months ago (#39 and the concurrent Kimi K2 experiment) and both stop at behavioral observation — no probe detectability, no external-vs-self signature comparison, no dosage/timing analysis exists anywhere in the corpus; the adjacent work covers different regimes (training-time compensation in #31/#82, external steering evaluation in #69/#75, self-report faithfulness in #53), leaving this intersection empty while being safety-critical (activation monitoring is a pillar of current safety cases), cheap to run on open weights, and informative whichever way the results go.

direction: Treat interpretability signals as endogenous rather than static — study how language models reorganize to evade internal monitors under training pressure, and establish causal coupling as the quantity that determines evasion cost.
project: Evasion Dynamics — The Moving-Target Problem for Mechanistic Monitors
question: When a model is fine-tuned under pressure to evade an internal monitor (linear probe, SAE feature, or steering-based detector), when and how does it re-route computation, and is evasion cost determined by the monitor's causal coupling to the behavior — such that causally load-bearing signals are expensive to decouple while merely correlational signals can be silenced at no capability loss?
first_experiment: Replicate and extend the lesion-during-training setup of item #72 — fine-tune Gemma-2-2B / Llama-3.2-3B on a two-hop geography task while suppressing its top monitor-aligned directions on every forward pass — tracking monitor AUROC ("monitor half-life"), task accuracy, and the ablation-causal load of the monitored direction across training; then measure generalization of the evasion by testing whether the adapted model also defeats the same probe refit at other layers, correlated SAE features, and probes for a different behavior (a compensation transfer matrix), with two controls: identical suppression without behavioral pressure, and suppression under a capability-preservation constraint, to cleanly test the coupling-cost prediction.
why: It converts a scattered cluster of independent 2026 findings — training against monitors (#9), lesion-induced compensation with mechanism explicitly left open (#72), performative self-reports (#30), and the repeated discovery that probing accuracy fails to predict causal importance (#2, #83, #88) — into a single testable law (evasion cost ∝ causal coupling) with metrics the field lacks; it is directly safety-critical, cheap to run with existing in-corpus infrastructure, and it has not been done because the only two precedents (#9, #72) are single-case, single-signal studies that each end by declaring mechanism and generalization open, while every other item treats monitors as static readouts of a frozen model rather than as targets of training pressure.

direction: Mechanistically characterize how models reorganize when trained under interpretability pressure (ablation, probe penalties, SAE-feature penalties), because the stability of interpretability artifacts across training is the untested assumption underlying every monitoring, auditing, and unlearning program, and only two preliminary 2026 posts touch it.
project: Where Does the Computation Go? A Mechanistic Taxonomy of Interpretability-Evasive Adaptation During Training
